Run command (README.md:30-35): `harbor run --dataset terminal-bench@2.0 --agent claude-code --model anthropic/claude-opus-4-1 --n-concurrent 4` (cloud via `--env daytona`). This session instead used `--path <local task dir>` to run single sample tasks directly against the already-pinned local clone (bypassing Harbor's own git-clone-on-demand step, which is otherwise identical for `--dataset`/`--registry-path` resolution).

Image build/pull: `should_use_prebuilt_docker_image()`, src/harbor/environments/definition.py:26-34 — returns True whenever task.toml sets `docker_image` (all 10 sample tasks do) and `--force-build` is not passed (CLI default is `--no-force-build`). So the OFFICIAL default run PULLS the prebuilt `ghcr.io/laude-institute/terminal-bench/<name>:2.0` image rather than building the task's own `environment/Dockerfile` locally — confirmed live (pull succeeded, ~5-10s per task, no local build triggered).

Per-task settings, uniform across all 10 sample tasks' task.toml: `[agent] timeout_sec = 900.0`, `[verifier] timeout_sec = 900.0`, `[environment] build_timeout_sec = 600.0`. CLI multipliers (`--timeout-multiplier`, `--agent-timeout-multiplier`, `--verifier-timeout-multiplier`, `--agent-setup-timeout-multiplier`, `--environment-build-timeout-multiplier`) all default 1.0 (`harbor run --help`, captured live). `-k/--n-attempts` default 1, `-n/--n-concurrent` default 4, `-r/--max-retries` default 0.

Prompt: `instruction.md`'s literal text is passed verbatim as the agent's instruction — confirmed live in trial.log, where pi was invoked with the exact instruction.md contents as its final positional argument; no separate Jinja prompt-template file is used for the base instruction (a `--user-prompt-template`/`--extra-instruction-path` exists for the OPTIONAL simulated-user / extra-instruction flows only, not exercised here).

Verifier/tests leak check (Q6): the Verifier class uploads `/tests` into the container only at verify time (src/harbor/verifier/verifier.py, upload ~line 182 `env_paths.tests_dir`; discovery/copy logic ~lines 120-206), and trial sequencing (src/harbor/trial/trial.py: agent.run() ~lines 489-700, `verifier.verify()` invoked afterward ~lines 882/952) shows the agent phase completes before the verifier phase starts — so in the default flow the test assertions are NOT visible to the agent while it works. Scoring: test.sh (boilerplate, editable per task) writes `1`/`0` (or a float) to `/logs/verifier/reward.txt`; `Verifier._parse_reward_text()` reads it and raises `RewardFileEmptyError` if empty. Pass criterion in every sample task inspected is binary reward==1.0 via a pytest exit-code check (`if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then echo 1 ... else echo 0`).

Agent CLI internals verified live: pi requires `--ak model_api=<style>` for any custom (non-native) base URL or raises `ValueError("Pi custom endpoints require the model_api agent argument")` (pi.py:224-226) — reproduced exactly. Valid values (`openai-completions`, `anthropic-messages`, etc.) come from pi's own installed docs (scratchpad/agents/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/models.md:54, docs/custom-provider.md). `--ak max_turns=N` writes a generated `max-turns.ts` Pi extension (pi.py:310-339) that aborts after N completed turns; with no `max_turns` set, turns are unbounded (bounded only by the 900s agent timeout).

Model network reachability (Q4): the task brief's premise that "opencode.py only sets baseURL for anthropic/google/openai providers" does not match the code read this session — model_connection.py's `PROVIDERS` table (lines 15-140) includes "openrouter" generically, used by every agent (including pi, opencode) whose `MODEL_CONNECTION = ModelConnectionSpec(passthrough=True)`. Verified LIVE that a `pi` trial in Harbor's default (bridge) docker network reaches an external recording proxy at the bridge gateway IP (`172.17.0.1:<port>`) via `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL`/`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` set with `--ae`, with NO `--network host` and no other network flag — a real model call was recorded end-to-end in the proxy's ledger.

Leaderboard "official"-ness (Q3): Harbor Hub leaderboards are self-reported — "Harbor Hub intentionally does not calculate row scores from linked trials, to enable maximally flexible leaderboard construction" (docs-mintlify/core-concepts/harbor-hub/leaderboards.mdx, read 2026-09-25). There is no central automatic score verifier; the closest thing to "official" is the pinned dataset commit (task.toml/instruction.md/tests/ unchanged) plus which reference agent adapter (pi.py/opencode.py/claude_code.py/codex.py) was used unmodified for install/run. A Vacant install step that only adds files inside the AGENT's own config/extension directory (not touching task.toml/instruction.md/tests/, and using the exact same `--agent pi --model ...` invocation) does not appear to violate anything Harbor itself enforces — though this is an inference from reading the leaderboard docs and adapter code, not a rule I found stated explicitly as "third-party hooks are allowed."

deep.unavoidable_differences:
1. **Sandbox-wide transparent TLS interception** (this research container specifically): ALL outbound HTTPS from a task container is MITM'd regardless of docker network mode or explicit proxy env vars — verified by reproducing the SAME "self-signed certificate" failure against pypi.org on a plain bridge-network container with nothing configured. Fixing it required mounting the sandbox's own CA bundle into every task container plus 3 separate env vars (SSL_CERT_FILE, CURL_CA_BUNDLE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS) covering curl/OpenSSL, Rust/rustls (uv), and Node (npm) separately — none of which are part of TB2.0's own protocol or Harbor's own CLI defaults. Any run in this environment must record these `--mounts`/`--ve`/`--ae` additions as environment-specific, not protocol-specific. On the owner's own machine this workaround should be unnecessary and must be re-verified absent.
2. **Prebuilt image tag, not digest pinning**: task.toml pins `ghcr.io/laude-institute/terminal-bench/<task>:2.0` by tag; registry.json pins the task-repo git commit, not the image's digest. Two runs months apart could in principle pull different image bytes behind the same tag without any error — record the image digest actually pulled (captured live via `docker pull` output) alongside every run's results.
3. **Single trial, `--n-concurrent 1`/`-n 1`**, vs. an official multi-seed run — this smoke used exactly 1 attempt per task; no variance/seed information was collected.
4. **Docker Hub rate-limiting (429)** blocked one exploratory `docker pull node:22-slim` from docker.io (unrelated to ghcr.io, which was never rate-limited) — worked around by letting pi's own nvm/npm bootstrap install Node inside the already-pulled ghcr.io task image instead of pulling a separate base image; record that this path (nvm-in-task-container) was used rather than a pre-baked Node image.
5. **Reduced task subset**: only 2 of the 10 sample tasks (regex-log, log-summary-date-ranges) were run to completion; qemu-alpine-ssh/qemu-startup were excluded entirely from this session's disk-usage survey due to their multi-hundred-MB ISO download + 32GB sparse-disk-image build steps, which were judged too risky for the shared 18GB container budget — any comparison claiming coverage of "the 10-task sample" must explicitly carve these 2 out or budget separately for them.
6. **Paid small model standing in for a local quantized model**: per the owner's 2026-09-25 09:30 UTC instruction, qwen/qwen3.5-9b pinned to a specific OpenRouter provider/quantization tag (darkbloom/fp4) was used through the recording proxy rather than a genuinely local llama.cpp/Ollama-served 9-12B model — network latency, provider-side rate limiting, and possible silent provider/quantization drift on OpenRouter's side are all differences from a truly local, fully reproducible inference stack; record the resolved provider tag on every logged call (the proxy ledger already does this).
7. **KS-1 template purity was not exercised in this smoke**: no Vacant hook/injection was actually installed into the pi container this session (out of scope for "official protocol" extraction) — the smoke establishes ONLY that the unmodified official pi adapter can reach a Vacant-shaped proxy and that pi has a sanctioned extension-file injection point (`--ak max_turns` mechanism); it does not itself demonstrate Vacant's actual hook running inside a Harbor container.
deep.vacant_attach:
Grounded in two live-verified facts plus one code-read fact, in increasing order of confidence:

1. (Live-verified) Harbor's OWN reference `pi` adapter already injects a generated extension file into the agent's config directory as a normal, sanctioned part of running it: `--ak max_turns=N` causes Harbor to write `max-turns.ts` into `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR` and pass `--extension <path>` on the pi CLI invocation BEFORE running the agent (pi.py:310-339, reproduced live in trial.log: `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=/tmp/harbor-pi-agent pi --print ... --extension /tmp/harbor-pi-agent/max-turns.ts <instruction>`). This is exactly the injection point a Vacant pi-extension needs — hooking pi's turn-end/tool-call events from inside pi's own extension API — and it requires ZERO changes to task.toml, instruction.md, or the verifier, since it happens entirely in the agent's own config directory during Harbor's normal "install" phase.
2. (Code-read) claude_code.py writes a `settings.json` into the container at a fixed remote path (claude_code.py:153 `_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH`, populated at lines 408 and 543-550) — this is the SAME class of file Vacant's own `adapters/hook.py` (per Vacant's repo map) already knows how to merge a hook config into for Claude Code's native Stop-hook mechanism, so a Vacant install step could append/merge into that same settings.json write, again without touching the task side.
3. (Inferred, not verified) OpenCode and Codex almost certainly have an analogous native config/plugin directory Harbor's opencode.py/codex.py already write into during install, but this session did not read those two files closely enough to name the exact path/mechanism — flagged as an open question requiring one more focused read before implementation.

Because Harbor Hub's leaderboards are explicitly self-reported and score-unverified by Harbor itself (docs-mintlify/core-concepts/harbor-hub/leaderboards.mdx: "Harbor Hub intentionally does not calculate row scores from linked trials"), and because the closest thing to a protocol constraint Harbor enforces is that the pinned task.toml/instruction.md/tests/ files and the reference `--agent <name>` adapter stay as-shipped, a Vacant install that only adds files inside the agent's OWN config/extension directory (as in point 1/2 above) — using the exact same `--agent pi --model <same>` (or claude-code/codex/opencode) CLI invocation Harbor would otherwise use — does not appear to change anything Harbor itself checks for "official." This is Harbor-specific: it says nothing about whether the task-owner's own separate benchmark rules (if run against the public tbench.ai leaderboard rather than a private Harbor Hub run) would treat an agent-side extension as in-bounds; that determination was out of scope for this session.

Arm B (reviewer-persona self-check, no Vacant evidence) vs Arm C (Vacant installed): both are naturally expressible as the SAME extension-injection mechanism with different payloads — Arm B's extension only appends a fixed persona-review prompt at turn-end (no trace/evidence block, matching Vacant's KS-1 requirement that B and C share every byte except the injected evidence block), Arm C's extension additionally reads Vacant's recorded trace (unread materials, unsourced specifics, ignored errors) and injects located feedback. Neither arm needs `--user-agent`/`--bridge` (Harbor's separate simulated-user machinery) since both operate entirely within the single target agent's own turn loop, not as a second conversational party.
deep.where_to_run:
This container was sufficient and appropriate for everything actually run this session: the 2 completed oracle/nop task pairs, the image-size survey of 8 of the 10 sample tasks, and the 1-task live pi smoke — all stayed within ~3.9GB peak disk (well under the 18GB shared budget) and used at most 1 concurrent container (n-concurrent=1), leaving the 4 CPU/15GB host comfortably idle otherwise.

This container is NOT recommended for: (a) the full 89-task terminal-bench@2.0 set (untested — per-task sizes unknown, likely several × the 10-task sample's footprint, and would need real `--n-concurrent`>1 to finish in reasonable time, which multiplies peak disk/CPU/RAM well past this session's tested envelope); (b) the 2 excluded qemu-* sample tasks, whose Dockerfiles download a large Alpine ISO and provision a 32GB sparse qcow2 disk at build time — these should be smoke-tested individually on the owner's machine (or a cloud env) with explicit disk headroom, not folded into a shared/batch run here; (c) any run needing multiple concurrent trials or multiple attempts (`-n`>1 / `-k`>1) for statistical signal, since this session only validated `-n 1 -k 1`; (d) anything requiring the sandbox's TLS-interception workaround to be silently "solved" rather than explicitly re-verified as absent — the owner's own machine should not need the `--mounts`/CA-bundle/env-var workaround documented here at all, and that should be confirmed with one quick oracle run there before trusting numbers from that machine either.

For the full 89-task set or any multi-seed run, Harbor natively supports `--env daytona` (a cloud sandbox provider) as documented in its own README — that is the more appropriate next step than scaling this container further.

corrected.claim: Report's headline finding: 'I did not find an opencode-specific narrowing on top of it [generic PROVIDERS/passthrough]... This directly CONTRADICTS the task brief's premise ("opencode.py only sets baseURL for anthropic/google/openai providers") — at this commit that is not what the code does.'
corrected.correct: opencode.py DOES contain exactly the narrowing the task brief's premise described, in a second mechanism the report never read. In `_build_register_config_command()` (opencode.py lines 546-552), the CONFIG-FILE baseURL override written into `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` is gated by `if base_url and provider in {"anthropic", "google", "openai"}:` — literally the three providers the original premise named. This does NOT contradict the report's other finding (MODEL_CONNECTION=passthrough=True at opencode.py:79, generic PROVIDERS table including openrouter) — that mechanism is real too, but it only produces environment variables (e.g. OPENROUTER_BASE_URL/OPENROUTER_API_KEY passed to the opencode subprocess via `env = dict(self.model_connection.env)` at line 593), not the config-file baseURL. Both are true simultaneously; the report should have said 'two separate mechanisms, one generic (env vars) and one narrowed to 3 providers (config file)' rather than declaring the original premise wrong. Practical upshot for the report's own open question 1: whether openrouter routing actually works through opencode for a proxy-substituted base URL depends on whether opencode's CLI itself honors a bare OPENROUTER_BASE_URL env var without the config-file override — that is still untested, not resolved by the code read either version performed.

corrected.claim: claude_code.py settings.json is cited as one uniform injection point via line refs '153/408/543-550', implying all three refer to writes of the same settings.json file.
corrected.correct: Lines 153 (path constant) and ~407 (upload call) do refer to the same file, `_REMOTE_SETTINGS_PATH` = `/tmp/claude-code-settings/settings.json`. Lines 543-550, however, write a DIFFERENT file: `{sessions_dir}/settings.json` under the separate ACP-adapter install path, containing only `{"model": model}`. deep.exact_protocol:
ORIGINAL harness (benchmark/benchmark.py in Aider-AI/aider @ 5dc9490): CLI defaults tries=2 (benchmark.py:199, -r/--tries), threads=1 (benchmark.py:200), num_tests=-1/all (benchmark.py:202), edit_format=None -> falls back to the model's own default edit_format (benchmark.py:815). Prompt = introduction.md(if any) + instructions.md + instructions.append.md(if any) + prompts.instructions_addendum.format(file_list=...) (benchmark.py:774-784; prompts.py has both templates verbatim). Retry: on failure, instructions = actual test stdout/stderr + prompts.test_failures.format(file_list=...) (benchmark.py:898-906) -- the model is shown real test output, not a synthetic hint. Per-unit-test-run timeout = 180s (benchmark.py:982, "timeout = 60 * 3"). Test commands by file extension (benchmark.py:985-992): pytest(.py), `cargo test -- --include-ignored`(.rs), `go test ./...`(.go), npm-test.sh(.js), cpp-test.sh(.cpp), `./gradlew test`(.java). Scoring (benchmark.py:468-567, summarize_results): pass_rate_1=%passing try 1, pass_rate_2=%passing by end of try 2 (headline leaderboard number), denominator=res.completed_tests (should=225). No paper/code divergence -- leaderboard YAML is generated straight from .aider.results.json runs of this exact script.
HARBOR ADAPTER protocol (adapters/aider_polyglot/{aider_polyglot.yaml, src/aider_polyglot/{adapter.py,utils.py}, src/aider_polyglot/task-template/{Dockerfile,test.sh,solve.sh,task.toml}}): n_attempts=1 in aider_polyglot.yaml -- Harbor's orchestrator does NOT reimplement aider's 2-try/test-failure loop; any retry is up to the agent's own turn budget. task.toml: agent/verifier timeout_sec=1800 (30min wall clock, not per-attempt). Task packaging (adapter.py::generate_task, _setup_workspace, _setup_test_files): environment/workspace/ (agent-visible: starter code + build files, NO test files) vs tests/ (verifier-only: .meta/config.json + real Exercism test file + rendered test.sh) -- confirmed empirically by generating 4 tasks and inspecting the tree; tests are genuinely hidden from the agent, only reached by the verifier mounting tests/ separately. Oracle: .oracle/solution.enc, AES-256-CBC+PBKDF2 via openssl, default password "tb-secret-please-change" (env ORACLE_SECRET overrides); solution/solve.sh decrypts+copies per a manifest.txt. Dockerfile (task-template/Dockerfile + utils.py::get_dockerfile_content): FROM buildpack-deps:jammy, then `apt-get install tmux asciinema curl`, then per-language block (python: add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes + python3.11; go: curl golang.org/dl tarball go1.21.5; java: openjdk-21-jdk; javascript: nodesource setup_20.x + global npm jest 29.6.4; rust: rustup; cpp: cmake+libboost-all-dev+libtbb-dev) -- every language's first RUN line is an apt-get against archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com.
Pass criterion (both harnesses): verifier/test.sh exit code 0 -> reward.txt=1, else 0; official leaderboard uses pass_rate_2 (2-try) as the headline metric, pass_rate_1 (1-try, no feedback) as the harder/stricter metric closer to what Harbor's bare n_attempts=1 protocol measures.

deep.agents:
Confirmed by reading src/harbor/src/harbor/models/agent/name.py (AgentName enum) and src/harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/{pi,opencode,claude_code,codex,aider}.py directly (all present at commit 6cb9ff3): Harbor has NATIVE installed-agent adapters for all four target agents -- AgentName.PI="pi", AgentName.OPENCODE="opencode", AgentName.CLAUDE_CODE="claude-code", AgentName.CODEX="codex" -- runnable exactly as the adapter README documents for claude-code, just swapping -a: `harbor run -d aider_polyglot -a pi -m "<model>"`, `-a opencode`, `-a codex`. There is ALSO a native AgentName.AIDER="aider" adapter (agents/installed/aider.py) that drives the real `aider` CLI with --reasoning-effort/--thinking-tokens/--cache-prompts/--auto-test exposed as Harbor options -- this is the true "run the original benchmark.py-equivalent protocol through Harbor" path for a reproduction anchor, without needing the fork repo (neginraoof/aider) the README's parity section names. mini_swe_agent.py also exists as a generic-scaffold fallback if wanted, but aider itself is Aider Polyglot's natural "official scaffold" so it's not needed here (unlike benchmarks with no native support).
Vacant hook point: identical to the general pattern other deep-dives found -- each installed agent is just a CLI binary Harbor execs inside the task's Docker container; Vacant would need to be inside that image (or bind-mounted in) with `vacant possess install` run against whichever of the four agents Harbor invokes, before the agent's turn starts, so the model endpoint it calls is Vacant's proxy. This is blocked here by the same apt-get/Docker-build issue (see smoke.result), not by anything specific to the Aider Polyglot protocol -- it's the generic "get Vacant into the Harbor task container" problem every benchmark in this study shares.
deep.vacant_attach: Not reachable in this container (Docker builds for aider_polyglot tasks are blocked at the first apt-get RUN line for all 6 languages -- see smoke.result). Design given the code read: (1) Vacant's own install path (`vacant possess install`, per CLAUDE.md's vrun/possess.py) writes proxy endpoint config into an agent's own persistent config file -- this needs to happen INSIDE the task's Docker image, either baked into a modified Dockerfile (COPY vacant binary + RUN vacant possess install as an extra layer before the workspace COPY) or bind-mounted via Harbor's environment config if it supports post-build mounts (not verified here -- would need reading harbor/src/harbor/environments/docker or equivalent, not done in this deep-dive's time budget). (2) Because environment/workspace/ (agent-visible) and tests/ (verifier-only) are already cleanly separated by the adapter (§2/packaging), Vacant's trace/recorder would see exactly the agent-editable file(s) and nothing else -- a clean, low-noise substrate for Vacant's unrecorded_change detection, better than benchmarks where agent and verifier share a directory. (3) Persona-check arm B (reviewer persona, no Vacant evidence) needs no code changes at all -- it is purely a second model-call added around the SAME agent output Harbor already produces, so it can be scripted at the orchestration layer without touching the adapter or Harbor core. (4) No `vacant possess install` install or persona-check code was actually run against a real container in this deep-dive -- this is a design read from the adapter+Harbor source, not an executed attach.
deep.cost_time:
Per-task (from the one real success we have, python_robot-name, qwen3.5-9b @ Darkbloom/fp4, $0.08/M prompt + $0.13/M completion per orq/qwen_qwen3.5-9b.json): 276 prompt + 679 completion tokens (553 reasoning) = 955 tokens total, $0.00011, 3.81s wall, 1 model call (passed first try). The failed go_hexadecimal call: 253 prompt + 2000 completion (all reasoning, 0 answer) = 2253 tokens, $0.00028, 8.24s, and would need at least one more (higher-budget or non-reasoning-model) retry to get an actual answer -- so realistic cost/task for this model is bimodal: ~$0.0001-0.0003 when it answers promptly, or 2-3x that plus a wasted call when it falls into the reasoning-repetition failure mode observed in 1 of 2 smoke tasks (50% in this tiny n=2 sample -- NOT a reliable rate estimate, but the mechanism reproduces across 3 sibling benchmarks' proxy logs so it is not a fluke).
Full 225-task set, best case (1 call/task like the passing smoke): 225 calls -- exceeds the 50 free-model-calls/UTC-day cap 4.5x, so cannot run in a single day on any free-tier-shaped cadence even ignoring the reasoning-loop failure mode; ~$0.03-0.06 in USD terms (225 x ~$0.0001-0.0003/task) which is trivially affordable -- the binding constraint is calls/day and the Docker/apt-get blocker, not USD. Realistic case accounting for retries/agent-loop overhead (not one-shot): 3-8 calls/task (cross-referenced against the sibling `try1-pi-qwen9b` ledger tag: 4 requests for one task under a real `pi` agent loop) -> 675-1800 calls for the full set, i.e. 14-36 days at the 50/day free cap, or fits in <1000/day only near the low end of that range.
Sensible subset for a demo: 20-30 tasks across all 6 languages (language choice does not change feasibility here since the Docker build never gets past the language-agnostic apt-get step) -> 60-240 calls at 3-8/task, comfortably under both the 50/day and 1000/day caps if spread across 2-5 days, and <$0.10 total even with the paid gpt-oss-20b fallback from MODELS.md (~$0.02-0.03/M input).
deep.unavoidable_differences:
1. No apt-mirror access from inside a Harbor task container in this sandbox (archive.ubuntu.com/security.ubuntu.com are not on the HTTPS-proxy allowlist, confirmed by reproducing "405 Method Not Allowed" on the first RUN line) -- blocks building ANY of the 6 language Docker images for this adapter, so no real Harbor-orchestrated, Docker-isolated agent run (of pi/opencode/claude-code/codex/aider) could be executed here at all; only a host-side substitute was run. Recorded in NOTES.md §3 + live_smoke.log (raw docker build failure output), not folded into any score.
2. The oracle/nop sanity check and the live model smoke both ran unit tests on the bare host (Python 3.11.15, Go 1.24.7) instead of inside the per-task container, so there is no filesystem/network isolation and the toolchain versions do not exactly match what the adapter's Dockerfiles pin (e.g. Go 1.21.5 in the Dockerfile vs 1.24.7 on host; python3.11 via deadsnakes PPA vs the host's existing python3.11.15) -- unlikely to change pass/fail for these particular exercises (pure algorithmic code, no OS-version-sensitive behavior) but not verified byte-for-byte against the containerized path.
3. The live model smoke used a hand-scripted one-shot/two-turn chat-completions loop imitating aider's benchmark.py protocol, not an actual Harbor `-a pi`/`-a aider` run driven through the real agent CLI (blocked by #1) -- a true agent-framework run would add tool-call scaffolding/system-prompt tokens this smoke did not spend, and would let the agent choose its own number of turns rather than the fixed 2-try schedule I imposed.
4. qwen/qwen3.5-9b (and the owner's stated gemma-3-12b-it preference) are both smaller than every model on the published leaderboard (smallest listed is 27B) -- any comparison to the YAML's numbers is extrapolation from the nearest size/family analogue (gemma-3-27b-it, 4.9% whole-format), not a reproduction, and the n=2-task live smoke here is far too small to estimate a rate at all (1/2 passed, with the 1 failure being a distinct "no answer produced" mode rather than a wrong answer).
5. Task directories were generated fresh, locally, from the pinned upstream polyglot-benchmark commit via the adapter's own main.py, not pulled from a Harbor-registry-published `datasets/aider_polyglot` artifact -- deterministic given the same commit, but not diffed byte-for-byte against a registry copy, and the default oracle-encryption secret ("tb-secret-please-change") was used rather than a rotated ORACLE_SECRET.
6. The reasoning-loop failure mode found in go_hexadecimal (model spends its entire output budget on visible chain-of-thought, produces zero answer tokens, reproduces identically at max_tokens=2000 and 6000) means whatever pass-rate number we eventually report for this model class will have a distinct, currently-unquantified "non-answer" failure bucket that the official harness's own error counters (num_malformed_responses, error_outputs, syntax/indentation_errors) were not designed to separate out from ordinary wrong-code failures -- worth a dedicated counter if this benchmark is used for the exhibition.
deep.where_to_run: This container cannot run the real Harbor-orchestrated protocol at all (Docker build blocked, §3/unavoidable_differences #1) -- confirmed, not assumed, by an actual build attempt. Two options going forward: (a) the owner's/lead's machine or a VM with unrestricted outbound apt access (even just to a Ubuntu mirror, not necessarily unrestricted internet) would unblock the Docker path entirely and let the real `harbor run -d aider_polyglot -a pi -m qwen/qwen3.5-9b` command run as documented; (b) if only this sandboxed environment is available, the host-side substitute demonstrated here (apply/skip the oracle, run the language's native test command directly, feed the raw pytest/go-test output back to the model exactly as benchmark.py's test_failures prompt does) is a workable, if less rigorous, stand-in that still exercises the real Exercism test suites and the real task packaging logic -- it should be labeled clearly as "host-side reproduction, not Docker-isolated" in any exhibit, per unavoidable_differences #2/#3. Given the disk/time budgets here were never actually the binding constraint (peak disk stayed at ~1GB of buildx cache, well under the 3-4GB budget, precisely because the build failed before pulling any language toolchain), moving this benchmark to a less-restricted machine is a network/proxy-allowlist fix, not a resource-budget fix.

deep.exact_protocol:
TWO distinct official protocols exist, not one — this is the central finding, see open_questions/unavoidable_differences too.

(A) Original repo's own harness (non-agentic; the NeurIPS-2024 paper's actual eval):
- Prompt: inference/prompt_format.py:1-31 (PROMPT_FORMAT_SINGLE — instruction, spreadsheet_path, spreadsheet_content = first --row=5 rows via pandas.DataFrame.to_string(), instruction_type, answer_position, output_path); multi-round ReAct variants at lines 33-95 add "{max_turn_num} rounds of interaction, two action types" text.
- Single-round driver: inference/inference_single.py — 1 LLM call, extracts fenced code (extract_code), executes once via code_exec_docker/ (persistent Jupyter kernel over HTTP, port 8081), then reruns the SAME code against test cases 2/3 by string-substituting filenames (model only ever sees test case 1).
- Multi-round driver: inference/inference_multiple.py, settings row_exec|react_exec|row_react_exec (scripts in inference/scripts/). Loop caps at --max_turn_num, default 5 (inference_multiple.py:138).
- Model call: inference/llm_api.py — plain openai.OpenAI(api_key, base_url).chat.completions.create(messages=..., model=...). No temperature/top_p/max_tokens/n set anywhere — provider default, single attempt, pass@1 only.
- Scoring: evaluation/evaluation.py:204-232, compare logic in compare_workbooks/cell_level_compare/compare_cell_value (lines 18-188): floats rounded to 2dp, Excel-epoch datetime conversion, ""≡None, exact type+value match otherwise. Note: the committed evaluation() function literally diffs answer.xlsx against the ORIGINAL input.xlsx (line 213-215, the real outputs/ path is commented out) — a repo placeholder bug, not something either benchmark run relies on; the shared compare_* functions are what matters and both original+Harbor use near-identical copies.
- Pass criteria: soft_restriction = fraction of 3 test cases passed, hard_restriction = all-or-nothing; verified_400 has 1 test case/task so soft==hard.
- Recalculation backend: evaluation/open_spreadsheet.py forces formula recalc before openpyxl reads cached values; LibreOffice 7.5+ (default non-Windows) or win32com+Excel (Windows). The win32com-only pipeline is what the 2024 paper used; LibreOffice support was added later via https://github.com/RUCKBReasoning/SpreadsheetBench/pull/32 (per README "Environment Setup" + Harbor adapter's cited "Modifications").

(B) Harbor adapter (agentic, file-based re-framing of the same dataset):

Source: Spreadsheet-RL, arXiv:2605.22642, "Spreadsheet-RL: Advancing Large Language Model Agents on Realistic Spreadsheet Tasks via Reinforcement Learning", Table 1 (caption: "Main Pass@1 results on SpreadsheetBench"; body text: "strictly follow this dataset's evaluation protocol", "912 unique tasks... each further instantiated into three... test cases" — confirms original 912 split, not verified_400). Read via https://arxiv.org/html/2605.22642, 2026-09-25. Numbers: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 9.3, Qwen3-4B 11.0, Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 (base) 12.0, Qwen3-14B 15.0, Qwen3-8B 15.9, Qwen3-32B 17.6; Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 +native harness 15.6, +tool access 19.3, +RL (Spreadsheet-RL-4B) 23.4. (Closed-model context only: GPT-4o 16.8, GPT-4o+Excel 18.4, o3 23.3, ChatGPT agent 35.3, Claude Files Opus 4.1 42.9, ChatGPT agent+.xlsx 45.5, Copilot Agent Mode 57.7.) This confirms the task brief's "9-18%" figure is accurate for Spreadsheet-RL's small non-RL Qwen3 checkpoints but on the WRONG split (912, not verified_400) — flag prominently. A WebSearch snippet surfaced a separate claim ("Claude Opus 4.6 34.89%... open-source 7.17%-17.14%") possibly from "SpreadsheetBench 2" (arXiv:2606.29955, a DIFFERENT newer benchmark, "end-to-end business spreadsheet workflows", not a new version of the same dataset) — I could NOT confirm via PDF/HTML fetch which split/benchmark that figure belongs to (tables were in compressed PDF streams, unreadable by my fetch tool); mark unverified, do not cite without re-checking the rendered table directly. The only same-split+same-harness number I have full confidence in is Harbor's own parity pair: claude-code@2.1.80+claude-haiku-4-5 = 68.83% (original-side fork, github.com/Rebabit/SpreadsheetBench@harbor-parity) vs 68.25% (Harbor adapter), n=3x400 — from adapters/spreadsheetbench-verified/README.md + parity_experiment.json — but this is a strong closed model, not a small open one, so it cannot serve as a small-open-model reproduction check.
deep.agents:
Confirmed directly (not from docs) via `harbor agent list` and `harbor agent schema pi` on this session's harbor checkout (commit 6cb9ff31): pi, opencode, claude-code, and codex are ALL present as native Harbor "installed agents" (harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/), among ~50 agents total. Harbor npm-installs each inside the task container and drives it via its own CLI (e.g. for pi: `pi --print --mode json --session-dir ... --provider

--model `), so it does not wrap or sandbox the agent's own tool-call loop in any way that would block Vacant's hook-every-tool-call mechanism — Vacant would install its hook into the agent's native config the same way it does outside Harbor. Read pi.py (harbor/src/harbor/agents/installed/pi.py) in full: it supports a fully custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint via ModelConnectionSpec(passthrough=True) + `--ak model_api=
deep.vacant_attach: Arm C (Vacant installed): the Harbor task boundary is exactly the agent's own container + tool-call loop — environment/ builds the container, the agent runs via its native CLI against /app/spreadsheets/1_{id}_input.xlsx and must produce /app/output/1_{id}_output.xlsx, then tests/test.sh (LibreOffice recalc + evaluate.py) runs completely afterward, untouched by the agent. Vacant attaches by installing its hook into the agent's own native config before `harbor run` starts the trial (or by layering a custom environment Dockerfile on top of task-template/environment/Dockerfile that pre-installs Vacant + the hook), letting it record every read/write/exec step, and letting its Stop-hook feedback loop fire before the agent's final turn — all strictly before test.sh/evaluate.py runs, so the benchmark's dataset files and scoring code are never touched. Arm C = identical `harbor run` invocation, same task.toml/Dockerfile/dataset/model, only the agent's own config additionally points at Vacant's hook. Arm B (reviewer-persona self-check, no Vacant evidence) = same again, but the only prompt/loop addition is an instruction to adopt an expert-spreadsheet-reviewer persona and re-check the output before finishing, with NO access to Vacant's recorded trace — the "intrinsic self-review, no external signal" condition the cited research (Huang et al. ICLR 2024; Tyen et al. ACL Findings 2024) predicts rarely helps. Concretely on this benchmark, grounded in what fired in my one real live trace: (a) "used the given materials" = did the agent actually openpyxl.load_workbook the real input file before writing values, vs. inventing them (Vacant traces "value sourced from a file read" vs "no traced source"); (b) "step justified" = does the final written cell range match the agent's OWN earlier-computed intermediate result (my live run: agent computed 9 correct matches in an intermediate tool call, wrote only 5 into the final file — a self-consistency gap fully visible in Vacant's trace without ever looking at the answer key); (c) "verify before delivery" = did the agent's own "let me verify the output" step (present in my trace) actually re-read and diff the FULL scored answer_position range against its own earlier values, or only a partial subset (in my trace: partial, missing exactly the rows that were wrong).
deep.cost_time: Per-task (this session's one live data point, pi + qwen/qwen3.5-9b via OpenRouter darkbloom/fp4, tag live-sbv-10452): 7 model calls, 85,116 prompt tokens, 4,546 completion tokens (1,807 reasoning), $0.00740, contributing to a 146s total trial wall time. No published per-task call/token numbers exist for this benchmark+agent+model combination (paper/Spreadsheet-RL don't release per-call trajectory logs; Harbor's own parity-run raw trajectories aren't bundled in the repo). Daily-cap math at 7 calls/task (single data point, not a distribution — real per-task call counts will vary with spreadsheet size/complexity): 50 free-calls/UTC-day cap => ~7 tasks/day => full 400-task set needs >=58 UTC days on free tier alone, not feasible for a full run, only small (5-10 task) daily subsets. 1000-calls/day cap => ~140 tasks/day => full set in ~3 days. In USD at $0.00740/task: full 400-task set ~$2.96; a 30-50 task subset ~$0.22-0.37. The other pinned paid candidate (google/gemma-3-12b-it @ deepinfra/bf16, $0.05/M in vs $0.15/M out) likely lands in a similar per-task cost range given similar token counts, but this was NOT run live to confirm — I judged the $0.15 cap better spent getting one full qwen3.5-9b data point with real tokens/cost/failure-mode than splitting it across two under-sampled models. These are pi-specific counts; OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex will very likely differ (different system-prompt/tool-schema overhead) — not measured, flagged as a gap.
deep.unavoidable_differences: 1) Harness identity: the only same-split, parity-verified number (claude-code+haiku-4.5, 68.83/68.25%) is on Harbor's AGENTIC adapter, already one step removed from the NeurIPS paper's own non-agentic completion-loop harness — any Vacant-vs-no-Vacant comparison inherits that same remove from the literal paper numbers; recorded honestly rather than presented as apples-to-apples with the paper. 2) Split mismatch: every small-open-model published number found (Spreadsheet-RL) is on the ORIGINAL 912-task split, not verified_400 — not directly comparable to a verified_400 run even before Vacant enters. 3) Sandbox-only infra workaround: this container's docker builds needed a CA-trust patch (COPY the sandbox's proxy CA bundle + ENV PIP_CERT/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, discovered because ALL container egress here is transparently TLS-intercepted regardless of docker network mode) not present in any published run's environment or in the owner's own exhibition machine — purely infra, touches zero task/dataset/scoring content, but is a real difference in provisioning; two temporary docker images created for this were deleted after use, confirmed via `docker images`/`docker ps -a` empty at session end. 4) Model/quantization: qwen/qwen3.5-9b pinned to OpenRouter provider/quantization darkbloom/fp4 (chosen to resemble a locally-run quantized small model per explicit owner instruction) does not correspond to any model/quantization combination in any published SpreadsheetBench table (published Qwen3 numbers don't specify inference stack/quantization beyond the bare model name). 5) Single-task, single-run live smoke: n=1 on 1 task, no variance estimate, only an existence proof that (a) the Vacant-relevant plumbing (pi + custom OpenAI endpoint + Harbor orchestration) works end-to-end on this exact benchmark, (b) real per-task cost/token numbers exist, (c) one concrete real (non-infra) failure mode was captured that is directly useful for designing the accountability-evidence checks arm C would run.
deep.where_to_run: Model-free grading (oracle positive/negative controls) and the Harbor CLI itself ran fine in this container (4 CPU/15GB RAM/no GPU, ~14-15GB free disk) — both oracle tasks completed in 67s total, well under the 2.5GB smoke budget once the accidental uv-dependency-group disk spike was caught and cleaned. The live pi+qwen3.5-9b smoke also ran here successfully through the lead's recording proxy (reachable via the docker bridge gateway 172.17.0.1:18900) after fixing the container-egress TLS-interception issue. For the FULL 400-task run (whether oracle-only for a fresh grader/parity check, or any real multi-task agent sweep), I'd recommend running on the owner's own machine or a dedicated VM rather than this shared, disk-constrained sandbox: (a) LibreOffice gets apt-get installed fresh in EVERY verifier container by test.sh (no image caching across tasks in the current adapter design), which is fine for 2 tasks but would add meaningful repeated network+CPU overhead at 400x; (b) this container's disk is shared with sibling research-agent sessions (confirmed disk pressure during this session from an unrelated `uv sync` default-group pull), so a full run risks starving others; (c) the TLS-interception workaround, while proven to work, is an extra moving part a clean run on real hardware doesn't need at all. The owner's own machine (or any machine with normal unfiltered internet) needs none of the infra fixes documented here and would reproduce this session's oracle/negative-control results identically (same pinned images, same evaluate.py).
deep.open_questions: 1) Which specific benchmark/split the "Claude Opus 4.6 34.89%, open-source 7.17-17.14%" figures (surfaced only via WebSearch snippet) actually belong to — SpreadsheetBench-2 (arXiv:2606.29955) or verified_400 — could not confirm from the PDF text extraction (tables in compressed streams); needs a direct fetch of the rendered HTML/table or manual PDF table extraction before citing. 2) Whether opencode/claude-code/codex's custom-model-endpoint wiring is really as uniform as pi's (I only fully read pi.py; a sibling's notes claim genericity across 40+ agents via MODEL_CONNECTION.passthrough=True but I did not independently verify claude_code.py/opencode.py/codex.py in this session) — worth a direct read before designing arm C/B for those three agents specifically. 3) No verified_400-specific small-open-model baseline exists publicly at all as of 2026-09-25 — is the owner OK with the comparison table citing 912-split numbers as directional context only (clearly labeled), or does this benchmark need to be deprioritized in favor of one with an actual same-split small-model baseline? 4) I ran only 1 live task on 1 model (qwen3.5-9b); whether the observed failure mode (correct read + correct intermediate computation + incomplete final write) is typical of small models on this benchmark or a one-off needs more than n=1 to say — a modest paid-tier sample (10-20 tasks, ~$0.15-0.30) would materially firm this up if budget allows in a follow-up session. 5) The 11-bug-fix claim and the 68.83/68.25% parity numbers are self-reported by the Harbor adapter's own authors (Rebecca Deng, Ryan Marten) in files they wrote — I confirmed the parsing-bug-fix code exists and looks correct by inspection, but did not re-run the full 400-task x3 parity experiment myself (that would cost real model spend at claude-haiku-4-5 pricing across 1200 trials, far outside this task's budget) to independently reproduce 68.83/68.25%.

Sampling: `--max-steps` default 10 (run.py:53); `max_tokens=3000` hardcoded for chat-path (utils.py:99), reasoning-path gets `max_completion_tokens=3000` (utils.py:85-86); NO temperature/top_p override anywhere -- whatever smolagents 1.3.0/litellm defaults to is what runs (exact default value unverified, the venv used to confirm this was deleted per disk budget before checking). `--concurrency` default 4 (ThreadPoolExecutor, run.py:145). custom_litellm.py:14-27: only the model-call itself is retried (tenacity, stop_after_attempt(450), exponential backoff) on Timeout/RateLimitError/APIConnectionError/InternalServerError -- not an answer-retry. Scoring: dabstep_benchmark/evaluation/scorer.py `question_scorer(a,b)`, verified by direct import + running it: strip+lowercase both sides; numeric-with-commas check first; else if either side has ';' or ',' -> order-insensitive list compare (recurses per element); else if both parse as bare floats -> numeric compare; else string compare (exact after depunctuation, or single-word subset match, or SequenceMatcher ratio>0.95). Numeric tolerance is rel_tol=1e-4/abs_tol=1e-4 (compare_numeric, confirmed by reading + exercising the function). Binary pass/fail per task, no partial credit, no pass@k. Harbor adapter (harbor/adapters/dabstep/adapter.py + template/, verified by building and actually running it this session, not just reading): renders task.toml/instruction.md/Dockerfile/solve.sh/test.sh via literal string .replace (no templating engine); instruction.md is HARBOR'S OWN prompt, materially different from the baseline's -- tells the agent to write the final answer to /app/answer.txt instead of calling smolagents' final_answer() tool, and uses a different framing sentence than either baseline prompt. task.toml: [verifier] timeout_sec=600, [agent] timeout_sec=1800, [environment] build_timeout_sec=600, cpus=1, memory=4G, storage=8G. Dockerfile: FROM ghcr.io/laude-institute/t-bench/ubuntu-24-04:20250624; apt-get python3-pip curl + pip3 install pandas; then 7 curl downloads of the context files from HF `resolve/main` (floating ref, not pinned -- can silently drift from what we pinned above) baked into the image at BUILD time. test.sh: reads /app/answer.txt first line, shells out to `python3 /tests/scorer.py "$agent_answer" "$expected_answer"`, writes 1/0 to /logs/verifier/reward.txt; missing answer.txt -> reward=0, exit 0 (not a harness error) -- verified directly (see smoke result below). solve.sh (the "oracle" agent) just cats the literal baked-in answer to /app/answer.txt. Critically: answers for the 450-task DEFAULT split are NOT ground truth -- run_adapter.py's extract_answers_from_task_scores() (file:line run_adapter.py:57-95) downloads the PUBLIC task_scores parquet (a leaderboard results table), keeps submissions with score==True, picks the shortest such string per task_id, and cleans it (strips markdown fences etc, run_adapter.py:29-49). Only the DEV split's 10 answers are the dataset's own true `answer` field (run_adapter.py:158-162). dabstep.yaml: n_attempts=1, orchestrator.n_concurrent_trials=1, default agent terminus-2 + claude-haiku-4-5.

deep.published_baselines: arXiv:2506.23719 Table 1 (fetched via WebFetch of the HTML rendering, 2026-09-25; table cell values extracted by the fetch tool's summarization, not independently re-verified against the raw PDF table -- flagged as secondary-source-extracted): o4-mini 76.39% easy/14.55% hard (best hard score in the paper); Claude 3.7 Sonnet 75.00%/13.76%; o3-mini 72.22%/13.76%; Llama 4 Maverick 75.00%/8.73%; Deepseek R1 68.21%/11.04%; Deepseek V3 66.67%/5.56%; Llama 3.3 70B 68.06%/3.70%; Llama 4 Scout 52.78%/1.85%; Llama 3.2 1B 1.39%/0.00% (weakest model in the table, and open-weight). No Qwen or Gemma model appears in the paper's table. Setting per the paper (also cross-checked against the baseline code): smolagents CodeAgent, ReAct-style, max 10 steps/task, hidden test set (i.e. the true, non-public grader -- distinct from the public leaderboard split we used for the smoke). Reproduction-check candidate: Llama 3.3 70B is the closest published open-weight anchor in the same rough capability tier as this project's target models, though still larger than the "local 12B-quantized" ceiling the owner wants; Llama 3.2 1B is the closest in size but is essentially at floor (0% hard) and not a useful discriminative anchor. Harbor's own adapter README parity table (harbor/adapters/dabstep/README.md, read directly): claude-code+claude-haiku-4-5, 130-task stratified sample (21 easy+109 hard, seed=42), 4 trials -- original benchmark (via a forked claude-code CLI repo, not the smolagents baseline) 37.69+-0.44% overall / 84.52+-1.19% easy / 28.67+-0.69% hard; Harbor adapter (terminus-2 agent) 36.92+-0.31% / 84.52+-1.19% (exact match) / 27.75+-0.44%. Neither side of this parity number is the smolagents baseline protocol -- both are Claude-Code-family agents in a terminal, a different action space than smolagents' Python-only sandbox -- so it is not directly comparable to the paper's Table 1 either.
deep.agents: No pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex adapter exists in the OFFICIAL DABstep repo -- the baseline IS a smolagents.CodeAgent loop calling a model in-process via LiteLLM; there is nothing CLI-agent-shaped to hook there in the traditional Vacant sense (no subprocess, no tool-call boundary a Stop-hook could wrap) -- the natural Vacant hook point would be smolagents' own step callback/memory API, not independently verified against the pinned smolagents 1.3.0 this pass. Harbor's own agent roster (checked via `harbor agent list` this session) includes claude-code, codex, and opencode (via an ACP shorthand `acp:opencode@<version>`); no `pi`-named entry was seen in the roster printed this session, but the harbor agents source was not exhaustively grepped for a pi adapter under another name, so absence is UNVERIFIED not confirmed. Harbor's own published parity experiment used `terminus-2` (Harbor's built-in terminal-driving agent) for the Harbor side and a forked `claude -p` CLI for the "original" side -- i.e. even Harbor's own validation doesn't exercise pi/OpenCode/Codex on this benchmark, only Claude-Code-family agents. For Vacant hook-ability specifically: harbor/adapters/{claude-code,codex,opencode} presumably shell out to the real CLIs (consistent with Vacant's existing adapters/agents.py translation table for those three), so hooking is plausible in principle, but doing so inside Harbor's docker task environment inherits the exact network-topology problem hit in the model-free smoke (task containers here cannot reach a host-bound proxy without --network host, which Harbor's docker environment does not appear to use for agent execution either -- same code path as the build). This needs a generic Harbor+Vacant network-reachability fix, not a DABstep-specific one, and is listed as an open question below rather than solved this pass.
deep.vacant_attach: Arm A (no Vacant): exactly the live smoke in section 3/4 above, unmodified official/adapter code. Arm B (reviewer-persona, no Vacant evidence): insert one extra model call after the agent's final answer is produced (after final_answer() in the baseline path, or after /app/answer.txt is written but before test.sh runs in the Harbor path) -- a reviewer-persona prompt sees only the question, guidelines, and the agent's own final answer/transcript, and may revise once; no external ground truth, no Vacant trace access; cheap (1 extra call/task). Predicted (per Huang et al. ICLR 2024 / Tyen et al. ACL Findings 2024, both already in scratchpad/study/src/) to rarely fix anything intrinsic since no new information is given -- the dabstep-70 live-smoke failure (misread manual.md's line-82 fee-band example as a fine threshold) is a good predicted-failure case for Arm B, since the reasoning reads as internally consistent on a second look with nothing pointing the model at the specific line it misused. Arm C (Vacant installed): the same reviewer-persona re-check call, but now grounded in Vacant's own trace evidence gathered for free from the agent's tool-call hook: (a) was manual.md opened at all before the final answer (binary, and per the smoke this is a RELIABLE signal for the 7/7 hard dev tasks but only 1/3 easy dev tasks -- the benchmark's easy/hard split is not the same partition as needs-the-manual, measured directly not assumed); (b) does every numeric literal in the final answer trace back to something actually read/computed in-session (a locate/blame-style check, matching Vacant's own trace/locate.py+blame.py design) vs. appearing with no antecedent -- this is exactly what would have caught the dabstep-70 failure (the 8.3% traces to a fee-band example string, not to any computation about a fine); (c) was fees.json/payments.csv opened when the question's wording implies they're needed (a cheap keyword heuristic, explicitly not a completeness guarantee, consistent with Vacant's own suitegauge.py "single-edge guarantee" framing). None of (a)-(c) requires knowing the gold answer -- exactly the owner's "was each step justified for this task" framing, not "is the output correct." Scoring stays untouched in both B and C: the (possibly revised) answer is written through the same path and graded by the same unmodified scorer.py; only what runs before that final write differs between arms.
deep.cost_time: This deep-dive's own spend (all read directly from the proxy's ledger/summary.json, never estimated): live-dabstep-5 4 calls / 14,255 tokens / $0.00120645; live-dabstep-70 8 calls / 81,933 tokens / $0.00673689; total $0.00794334 across 12 calls, against the $0.15/2-task budget given (used ~5%). Per-task extrapolation for the full protocol: official baseline caps steps at 10/task; our one manual-requiring task used 8/10 steps and its LAST call alone carried 78k cumulative prompt tokens (smolagents' CodeAgent keeps the full growing transcript in context each step) -- hard tasks, which structurally need 2+ files cross-referenced (fee IDs, account types, ACI codes per section on exact_protocol), should be assumed close to the 10-step ceiling, not the 4-step easy-task floor. 50 free-calls/day cap (MODELS.md): even at a conservative 10 calls/task that is 5 tasks/day -- the 450-task default split would take ~90 days, the 10-task dev split ~2 days; the free tier is INFEASIBLE for anything beyond a handful of demo tasks/day, which is why MODELS.md's UPDATE already moved to a paid-but-cheap pinned model (qwen/qwen3.5-9b @ darkbloom/fp4, $0.08/$0.13 per M in/out tokens) -- consistent with the owner's own instruction in this task to use paid budget rather than free-tier for anything beyond isolated smoke calls. 1000-calls/day tier (unverified exact unlock threshold per MODELS.md's own flag): ~100 tasks/day at 10 calls/task -- 450-task split in ~4.5 days, the 130-task Harbor parity sample in ~1.3 days. USD extrapolation (n=1, explicitly flagged as an extrapolation not a measurement): easy/light tasks ~$0.001-0.002/task, manual-heavy tasks ~$0.007/task measured; hard tasks likely higher still given the near-ceiling step count and growing-transcript cost structure -- a rough guess of $0.01-0.02/task for the 378 hard tasks puts a full default-split run at roughly $4-8 on qwen/qwen3.5-9b, but this needs a 20-30 task pilot across both difficulty levels before committing real budget to it, which was not done this pass (budget/time). No published per-task calls/tokens numbers were found for DABstep -- the paper reports accuracy only in the portion fetched, and the public `submissions` HF parquet split (queried directly, 74,970 rows) carries agent_answer strings but empty reasoning_trace fields in the rows sampled, so it is not a usable source for calls/tokens, only for characterizing the leaderboard's (low) data quality.
deep.unavoidable_differences: (1) Answer source: 444 of 450 default-split answers are the shortest publicly-accepted leaderboard submission, not true ground truth, and the leaderboard itself is public/unauthenticated and low-trust (sampled directly this session: submission_id/organisation fields contain garbled embedded free text like "sz-s"/"user speta") -- any score against the default split conflates "matched the true answer" with "matched a previously accepted string"; only the 10 dev-split answers are real gold. Recommendation: headline off the 10-task dev split, caveat the 450-task default split's answers every time cited, exactly as anticipated by the task's own question 1. (2) Harbor's instruction.md prompt is not the baseline's prompt (write-to-file vs. tool-call, different framing) -- a Vacant-vs-no-Vacant comparison run through Harbor is not directly comparable to a number quoted from the original DABstep leaderboard, and must say so. (3) Model: neither the paper's Table 1 nor Harbor's own parity baseline used qwen/qwen3.5-9b or google/gemma-3-12b-it; closest published small-model anchors are Llama 3.2 1B (near floor, not discriminative) or Llama 3.3 70B (larger than the target "12B-quantized" tier). (4) Exact reproduction of the baseline needs smolagents==1.3.0 pinned to transformers==4.47.1 (the latter undocumented by DABstep's own requirements.txt, discovered by trial and error this session) -- current smolagents (1.26.0) has REMOVED the system_prompt constructor kwarg and CODE_SYSTEM_PROMPT export the baseline relies on, so an unpinned install is not runnable at all, and a pinned install is running materially different CodeAgent internals across versions even with byte-identical prompts. (5) The model-free oracle smoke used a hand-patched Dockerfile (proxy ENV vars, CA bundle, http->https apt mirror rewrite) and manual `docker build --network host` instead of the official `harbor trial start` invocation, because Harbor's own buildx build cannot reach this sandbox's loopback-only proxy -- this proves the grading mechanism (test.sh/scorer.py) is correct and unmodified, but is not evidence that the official CLI invocation runs cleanly end-to-end here; documented as a sandbox network-topology limitation, not a benchmark-level finding, and would need re-checking on whatever machine actually runs the exhibition/pre-registered batch. (6) No hard-task live smoke was run (time/call budget) -- all hard-task calls/tokens/cost figures in the cost_time section are extrapolated from a single manual-heavy easy task, not measured; flagged everywhere it's used. (7) Concurrency: official baseline runs 4 tasks in parallel by default; a sequential Vacant-side run changes wall-clock throughput only, not per-task correctness/cost, so this affects only time comparisons. (8) Process note, not a benchmark-protocol difference but worth recording: this session's `docker builder prune -f` cleanup reclaimed some buildx cache entries that pre-dated this session (shared daemon, other agents in this container) -- no other agent's named image was deleted (verified: docker images was empty of anything before and after that wasn't built here), but a filtered prune would have been the more careful choice and is what should be used next time a benchmark study needs docker cleanup on this shared host.
deep.where_to_run: This sandbox container is adequate for protocol study, code reading, dataset pinning, model-free grading verification (achieved, both easy and hard dev tasks), and small live-model smoke tests through the recording proxy (achieved, 2 tasks, $0.008 total) -- all within the given 4 CPU/15GB RAM/shared-disk limits and well under the 4GB peak-disk budget (peaked at ~1.9GB, cleaned back to baseline). It is NOT adequate for running the official `harbor trial start` CLI end-to-end unmodified, because Harbor's docker-build path cannot reach this sandbox's loopback-only egress proxy (network-topology limitation of this environment, not of Harbor or DABstep) -- confirmed by direct bridge-vs-host-network reachability tests, and worked around only by hand-patching a copy of the generated Dockerfile and building manually outside Harbor's own orchestration. A pre-registered batch run (the 450-task default split, or even the 130-task Harbor parity sample) at the volumes discussed in cost_time (needing sustained docker-build network access AND potentially many hours of wall time at ~10 calls/hard-task) should run on the owner's own machine or a VM with normal (non-proxied, non-loopback-restricted) outbound network -- exactly where the exhibition's own machines would need to run this kind of check anyway, per this repo's own "physical exhibition, offline-capable, no dependence on a fragile sandboxed proxy" constraints. This sandbox remains the right place for iterating on the Vacant-hook design (arm B/C wrapper logic, prompt/trace plumbing) using the model-free oracle and the 10-task dev split's already-verified grading path, before moving to a real machine for volume.
deep.open_questions: (1) Fidelity: is the owner's call on default-split vs dev-split-only confirmed -- given the default split's leaderboard-extracted answers and the low-quality public submissions data found here, should ANY reported number for this project use the 450-task default split at all, or should DABstep usage here be capped at the 10-task dev split (true gold) plus a hand-picked stratified sample whose answers are independently re-derivable (e.g. via oracle cross-check against the actual data files, as done for dabstep-5/49/70)? (2) Does the project want to pursue an official-leaderboard submission path (needs an HF account per the task's own framing) to get hidden-grader numbers, or is that out of scope given the "no submission, exhibition only" mandate in this repo's CLAUDE.md? (3) Which prompt should a Vacant-instrumented run actually use -- the baseline's (final_answer() tool call, truer to the paper's own numbers) or Harbor's (write-to-file, needed if driving pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex through Harbor's existing agent adapters) -- these are not swappable without affecting comparability to either published source, and the choice determines whether Vacant hooks into a Harbor docker container or a bare smolagents Python process. (4) A generic fix for Vacant-inside-Harbor-docker network reachability was identified as a blocker but not solved this pass (affects every Harbor-run benchmark, not just DABstep) -- is that fix in scope for this study, or a separate infrastructure task? (5) The hard-task calls/tokens/cost extrapolation in cost_time is explicitly n=1-derived and needs a small (20-30 task) pilot across both difficulty levels to tighten before committing real budget to a full run -- worth doing before any pre-registered batch. (6) Whether smolagents==1.3.0/transformers==4.47.1 is an acceptable "exact official protocol" pin for a from-scratch Vacant-wrapped harness, or whether the project should instead standardize on Harbor's already-parity-checked path (terminus-2-style) despite it using a different prompt/action-space than the paper. (7) DABstep-v2: the HF Space's own content.py (read locally) says "DABStep-v2 launching in the coming weeks" as of the pinned commit, and separately says "Validation requests are closed" for the current leaderboard -- worth a follow-up check closer to any pre-registered run date, since a v2 launch mid-project could shift which split/version is "current" by the time of the exhibition.

pick.name: GDPval gold subset (openai/gdpval, 220 tasks; community harness inspect_evals gdpval)
pick.why: This is the only public benchmark that literally matches the owner's marketing-plan example: an occupation-realistic prompt, reference files (spreadsheets, PDFs, decks) and a professional deliverable. Each task ships gold deliverable_files plus rubric_json / rubric_pretty (HF dataset card, read 2026-09-25). That makes it the best source of 'given materials, produce a deliverable' tasks for an exhibition side-by-side. It is NOT deterministically gradable: the official grading is blind expert pairwise comparison, and the automated grader is OpenAI-hosted (GPT-5 judge via evals.openai.com, which needs an account), so it cannot be run offline. Any local rubric scoring with a small judge would be our own non-official measure and must be labelled that way.

deep.exact_protocol: gdpval.py:19-57 Task: solver=[use_tools([bash(180),python(180)]), generate(), extract_deliverable_files()]; scorer=exact() (only captures final text as deliverable_text, not a correctness scorer); sandbox=("docker", Dockerfile). deep.published_baselines: Official (OpenAI paper arXiv:2510.04374 §3.1, ar5iv text extraction read 2026-09-25): models evaluated were GPT-4o, o4-mini, o3, GPT-5, Claude Opus 4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Grok 4 — ALL frontier/closed. No open-weight model and NO model ≤35B was evaluated by OpenAI in the paper. 3 samples/prompt, 3 human graders/sample (9 comparisons/prompt/model). Human baseline exact figures: H_T=404min mean completion time, H_C=$361 mean completion cost, R_T=109min review time, R_C=$86 review cost (paper §3.2). Automated grader: 66% agreement w/ human graders vs 71% human inter-rater agreement (paper + inspect_evals README, both quote this). inspect_evals' OWN replication (src/inspect_evals/gdpval/README.md:77-89): GPT-5 thinking=low via this exact harness → 47.3%±6.2% avg score, 219/220 graded (1 errored: OpenAI Responses API 3600s timeout). CRITICAL CAVEAT the README itself states: OpenAI's own official leaderboard score for nominally the same GPT-5 release is 31.9% (wins-only)/34.6% (wins+ties) — a large gap vs the harness's 47.3%, i.e. even this community harness's own numbers for the flagship model are NOT a clean reproduction of the official leaderboard. Small open-weight (≤35B): no official OpenAI numbers exist anywhere. Only published numbers found: Artificial Analysis' "GDPval-AA v2.1" (artificialanalysis.ai/evaluations/gdpval-aa, read 2026-09-25) — an INDEPENDENTLY-RUN, methodologically DIFFERENT benchmark (same task set, but scored via AA's own blind-pairwise-LLM-judge → Elo rating, NOT OpenAI's win-rate-vs-human-expert metric, NOT submitted to evals.openai.com, NOT the OpenAI GPT-5 judge). Elo scores ≤35B (2026-09-25): Qwen3.8 27B (xhigh) 1409, (medium) 1368, (low) 1342; Gemma 4 31B (Reasoning) 606; Gemma 4 26B-A4B (Reasoning) 553; Gemma 4 12B (Reasoning) 413; Qwen3.5 9B (Reasoning) 407; IBM Granite 4.2 30B 564. These are NOT comparable to OpenAI win-rate numbers — different grader/scale/methodology, must be cited as "GDPval-AA (Artificial Analysis variant)" never as "GDPval score". No reproduction-check candidate exists using the exact official protocol for any small open model — closest is inspect_evals' own GPT-5 run, which itself already diverges from the official number as noted above.
deep.agents: The gdpval Task's solver is Inspect's OWN native tool-loop (use_tools([bash,python])→generate()→extract_deliverable_files()) — the model is called directly via Inspect's ModelAPI/HTTP, and Inspect's own Python executes bash/python tool calls inside the sandbox. NO subprocess invocation of pi, OpenCode, Claude Code, or Codex anywhere in gdpval.py/util.py, and grepping the WHOLE inspect_evals repo for "claude code"/"opencode"/"codex"/"mini-swe"/"terminus" found no CLI-agent integration pattern anywhere (the one hit, ipi_coding_agent, only mentions Claude Code/Copilot/Cursor in prose as the class of agent its prompt-injection benchmark models; its own solver is likewise Inspect's native generate() loop, not a real CLI agent). HOWEVER inspect_ai core v0.3.268 DOES ship a generic external-agent bridge — inspect_ai.agent.AgentBridge / sandbox_agent_bridge / human_cli (confirmed present via `python -c "import inspect_ai.agent as a; dir(a)"`) — designed to let an actual external agent process running inside the sandbox, speaking an OpenAI-compatible API back to Inspect, drive the task instead of Inspect's own loop. gdpval does NOT use this bridge today. Retrofitting pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex onto gdpval means writing a custom solver that (a) installs the chosen CLI agent inside the sandbox image, (b) launches it headless pointed at the bridge endpoint, (c) collects deliverable_files/ the same way — plausible but nontrivial, not a drop-in swap. No official scaffold (mini-swe-agent, Terminus) is used by gdpval either — it's 100% Inspect-native.
deep.vacant_attach: Vacant hooks a real CLI agent process's tool calls; since the official gdpval protocol calls the model directly with no CLI-agent process to attach to, Vacant CANNOT attach to "official" runs as shipped — the only path is the §agents retrofit (custom solver running pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex headless inside the sandbox via the AgentBridge, where Vacant's `vacant do`/`vacant hook` then apply exactly as for any other headless CLI run). Arm A (control) = unmodified official solver chain. Arm B (reviewer-persona, no Vacant) = insert one extra generate() step between generate() and extract_deliverable_files() that re-prompts the SAME model with a skeptical-QA persona + its own deliverable_files, asking it to revise — cheap, no new infra, but has no file-provenance/grounding signal, i.e. exactly the "intrinsic self-review, no external signal" condition Huang et al./Tyen et al. predict rarely helps. Arm C (Vacant installed) = the CLI-agent retrofit above, with Vacant's Stop-hook feedback wired to check: did the agent's bash/python history ever read/parse each reference_files/ entry before citing it in a claim (Vacant's trace/locate.py+blame.py already do exactly this value→first-written-step trace, applicable unmodified) → any unsourced numeric/date/named-entity claim in deliverable_text or the deliverable files gets flagged and sent back before delivery. Direct confirmation this maps onto real GDPval judging: pulled actual rubric_json for 3 gold tasks (110 rubric items total across them) and found items like task 0ed38524's "Every issue or theme named in the talking points appears in the ECID Constituent Feedback Tracking Log.xlsx (in any district) and is not fabricated" and "Any quantitative references... match figures computable from [the reference log]" — these are EXACTLY the "unsourced specifics in a deliverable" accountability-point failure mode from the owner's own marketing-plan example, independently validated by the benchmark's own real rubrics, not invented for this study. Manual classification of the 3 tasks' rubric items (38+44+28=110 total, task_ids 83d10b06/17111c03/0ed38524): roughly half are mechanically script-checkable (file format/filename/worksheet name/literal value presence/page count/merged-cells/fill-color — e.g. ~33/38, ~18/44, ~5/28 by task) and roughly half require semantic/paraphrase-tolerant judgment ("wording can vary but must clearly convey...", cross-document fact matching, "overall formatting and style" aesthetics) — even the "mechanical" half often still needs fuzzy/semantic tolerance, so a naive keyword scorer would systematically over- or under-score; this is a genuine finding from real rubric text, not an estimate, though the mechanical/judgment split itself is a manual heuristic classification (boundary cases exist) rather than an automated, reproducible count.
deep.cost_time: No official per-task tool-call/token count published anywhere found (paper, inspect_evals README, jeqcho replication dataset card) — flagged unverified, not guessed. Paper only gives aggregate human-vs-model time/cost (§3.2 H_T/H_C/R_T/R_C above) and states OpenAI's own frontier runs used web-search + code-interpreter tools with background sampling, plus a best-of-N=4 prompt-tuning variant — neither gives a call count. What THIS run actually measured (real billed data, 1 task, non-official minimal sandbox, turn-limited to 8): 8 model calls, 23,640 prompt + 1,392 completion tokens, $0.00207216, 42.2s wall — and the agent had NOT yet started writing anything by call 8, still in file-discovery/dependency-troubleshooting (blocked by the sandbox substitution, not by task difficulty per se). This is strong evidence a REAL attempt (full office/data-science toolchain available) needs well more than 8 turns — the paper's own unused 5-step "Mandatory formatting checks" prompt block implies dozens of turns for a serious attempt (convert-to-PNG, inspect each page, write programmatic checks, re-verify, repeated). Under 50 free-calls/UTC-day (MODELS.md): a single task can plausibly consume the entire daily quota alone at a conservative 10-20 calls/task estimate; a 220-task full run is not feasible on free tier (would take weeks even ignoring free-endpoint volatility MODELS.md already flags). Under 1000 calls/day: ~30-100 tasks/day at an estimated 10-30 calls/task — a meaningful subset, not the full 220. In USD (paid fallbacks per MODELS.md): this truncated task cost $0.00207 for 8 calls/~25k tokens on qwen3.5-9b; a COMPLETED task (real deliverables, multi-file reads, formatting-check iterations) would plausibly use 5-20x the tokens — order-of-magnitude $0.01-0.05/task, so a 10-30 task subset ($0.10-1.50) fits comfortably in the owner's $5 budget, and even the full 220-task gold set is plausibly $2-15 on these cheap models — but this is an estimate extrapolated from a truncated run, not a measurement, and is moot regardless because disk (not USD) is the binding constraint preventing the official sandbox from running here at all.
deep.unavoidable_differences: (1) SANDBOX: ran a 187MB minimal substitute (python:3.11-slim, no office/data-science stack) instead of the official ~5-8GB Dockerfile (147 packages incl. torch/LibreOffice/JRE/etc.), because the official image's estimated size (torch wheel alone 906.5MB, ~1.1GB for just the 18 heaviest packages compressed, README warns "up to 10 minutes to build") exceeds this run's 3-4GB smoke budget and the ~13-18GB disk shared with sibling agents. DEMONSTRATED CONSEQUENCE (live run): a real model in the substitute sandbox cannot read the .xlsx reference file at all (no openpyxl/xlrd/LibreOffice, no network to pip-install them — Inspect's own Docker sandbox launch does not route through this container's $HTTPS_PROXY). Any score from this substitute sandbox would be artificially near-zero regardless of model quality and must never be compared to a real run — this run only used it to prove harness PLUMBING (file mounting, tool execution, deliverable export, table consolidation), not task-completion capability. (2) DATASET REVISION: to see rubric_json/gold deliverable_files at all one must diverge from the harness's pinned a3848a2a8... revision (predates those columns) to `main` — the harness AS CHECKED OUT literally cannot do local rubric scoring. (3) GRADING: the official metric (blind pairwise win-rate vs human expert, graded by evals.openai.com) cannot run here at all — no account/API access exists in this environment, and no sign-ups/web-forms are permitted; WebFetch on evals.openai.com only returned an empty client-rendered React shell so even its login requirement could not be confirmed either way (flagged unverified). Any local rubric-based score would be a different, non-official measure and must be labeled as such — none was built in this smoke (out of scope). (4) TURN/MESSAGE/TIME CAPS: official protocol sets none by default; this run added --turn-limit 8 purely to bound cost/time, which is why the live task did not finish — not a reflection of task difficulty alone. (5) MODEL: qwen/qwen3.5-9b (9B fp4, provider darkbloom/fp4) vs the paper's GPT-4o/o4-mini/o3/GPT-5/Claude Opus 4.1/Gemini 2.5 Pro/Grok 4 — zero scale/openness overlap; intentional per owner instruction, but means no numeric comparison to the paper's headline results is meaningful. (6) PROMPT: used the harness's actual default DEFAULT_PROMPT_SUFFIX as shipped; did NOT add the paper's own mandatory 5-step formatting-check block (PROMPT_ELICIT_CAPABILITIES_SUFFIX) since the harness itself doesn't wire it in by default — faithful to "run it exactly as the repo does" but that itself already diverges from what the paper's OpenAI-model runs were given (documented gap in the harness, not introduced by us). (7) SAMPLING: no reasoning-effort/temperature control applied, used proxy/OpenRouter defaults — the paper's own low/medium/high reasoning-effort ablation has no analogue tested. (8) TOOLS: paper's OpenAI-model runs had hosted web-search + OpenAI Responses-API code-interpreter with background sampling; Inspect's gdpval task explicitly substitutes generic bash+python tools instead (README §Notes says so itself) — inherited, not an extra deviation we introduced, but real nonetheless.
deep.where_to_run: This container: ran the model-free harness install, dataset inspection, rubric parsing, and BOTH smoke steps (mockllm plumbing test + live qwen3.5-9b test) directly here, using a deliberately minimal substitute Docker sandbox — total footprint ~0.9GB, well within the 3-4GB budget, all Docker images cleaned up after each step (`docker images` empty at end). Did NOT build the official ~5-8GB Dockerfile here at all (judged infeasible for this container's disk budget given the shared ~13-18GB free disk with sibling agents) — that would need either a machine/VM with materially more free disk headroom (the owner's own machine, or a purpose-provisioned VM with ≥15-20GB free just for this one benchmark) OR accepting the official image never gets pre-built here and instead letting Inspect build-on-first-run there (same size problem, just deferred). Given GDPval's per-task 114s-class real-model latency is irrelevant to the exhibition's stated hard requirement (Vacant CLAUDE.md: exhibition needs seconds-level interaction, mechanism-simulation only) and its grading is off-container anyway (evals.openai.com), GDPval is best treated as a background/offline benchmark-comparison run (owner's own machine or a dedicated VM, not this shared container), never as a live exhibition component.
deep.open_questions: (1) Whether evals.openai.com/gdpval/grading requires an OpenAI account/login to submit a run — WebFetch only returned the empty client-rendered shell, could not confirm either way without executing the page's JS or attempting a real submission (out of scope here, no sign-ups permitted). (2) No verified per-task call/token count from any real, non-truncated GDPval agent trajectory exists anywhere found — all §cost_time numbers beyond the raw measured $0.00207/8-calls/42.2s figure are order-of-magnitude estimates, explicitly labeled as such, not measurements. (3) Exact HF-account/session requirements for `-T upload_to_hf=True` not tested (would need a real HF token; out of scope, no credential use permitted). (4) The mechanical-vs-judgment rubric-item classification (§agents/vacant_attach) is a manual heuristic count over 3 tasks' 110 items, not an automated/reproducible script — a real local-scorer feasibility study would need to formalize and validate that classifier, and check its agreement with the gold deliverable (scores near max) vs an empty/random deliverable (scores near 0), which this smoke did not attempt (out of scope for a model-free/turn-limited smoke). (5) Whether the officially-built 5-8GB sandbox, if built on a machine with adequate disk, would let a small open model (qwen3.5-9b / gemma-3-12b) actually COMPLETE a GDPval task at all within a reasonable turn budget is untested — this run's live smoke only demonstrates the *substitute* sandbox's predictable failure mode, not the official sandbox's real difficulty for a 9-12B model.
