Cloned repos for further reading under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Vacant/95e2b6b6-418f-504c-a59e-fd594ef13041/scratchpad/study/src/{harbor,SWE-bench,mini-swe-agent,multi-swe-bench,evalplus,polyglot-benchmark,LiveCodeBench}. No Docker images pulled or built by me; no OpenRouter/model calls made (per instructions, only the lead calls models); total added disk ~231MB (well inside the shared ~18GB budget).

candidates.name: GDPval (OpenAI)
candidates.task_shape: 220 'gold subset' tasks (5 per occupation x 44 occupations, top 9 GDP sectors). Each = realistic prompt + reference files (spreadsheets, PDFs, slide decks, audio/video, CAD) + context, mirroring a real professional deliverable. 17 reference files in gold subset. This is the single closest public analogue to the prompt's own marketing-plan-with-logo-schedule-data example. Agent workspace via inspect-evals: bash+python tools in a Docker sandbox, step count agent-driven/unbounded.
candidates.grading: Primary metric is blind human-expert pairwise comparison. An 'automated grader' exists but is a hosted OpenAI service, not local code: per inspect_evals docs it runs pairwise comparison against golden human solutions using GPT-5 with tools, 3x for variance, 95% CI bootstrap -- results must be uploaded to HuggingFace and submitted through evals.openai.com/gdpval/grading. No offline/local grading path exists. Automated-grader/human agreement ~66% on gold subset per OpenAI's own resources page.
candidates.official_protocol: Official: OpenAI's own eval + submission-based automated grader (GPT-5 judge, non-local). Community: inspect-evals[gdpval] package wraps it as an Inspect AI task; default solver is Inspect's generic tool-calling solve() but accepts any Solver; for OpenAI models the original paper enabled web_search + code_interpreter tools. Docker sandbox required, image build ~10 min; validated on an EC2 t3.2xlarge (8vCPU/32GB), no number given for smaller boxes.
candidates.size_and_versions: HF dataset openai/gdpval, 2.29GB, 11 commits, latest 'Release GDPval v2 (rubrics + deliverables)' ~7 months before 2026-09-25 read date. Gold subset = 220 tasks; full set has 38 reference files.
candidates.requirements: Docker sandbox for the agent run; HuggingFace account + upload for grading; ultimately a web submission to OpenAI's own grading endpoint (network + account dependency, no offline mode). License: dataset appears open on HF (no explicit license text captured this pass -- unverified).
candidates.supported_agents: Any tool-calling agent via Inspect's Solver interface in principle; no documented first-class pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex adapter (would need custom Inspect Solver wrapper, analogous to Harbor's installed-agent wrappers for coding benchmarks).
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not found -- GDPval's public results focus on frontier models (GPT-5, Claude, Gemini families) in the original paper; no small-open-weight (<=35B) numbers surfaced in this pass. Unverified whether any exist.
candidates.fit: Best conceptual match to the owner's own worked example (real materials -> real deliverable, accountability = did the agent use what was given). But because self-review/self-verification would have to be checked against Vacant's trace rather than GDPval's own grader (which is external and paid), this benchmark mainly supplies realistic task *shapes and materials*, not a runnable free-tier grading loop.
candidates.cost_time: Unmeasured/unbounded per-task model-call count (agent decides how many tool calls to open/read multi-MB reference files and produce a deliverable) -- a handful of tasks could plausibly exhaust the 50 free-calls/UTC-day OpenRouter budget on the agent side alone, before any judging. Judging itself costs nothing against the local budget (it's an external paid GPT-5 call on OpenAI's side) but requires a network round-trip and cannot be run air-gapped for the exhibition.
candidates.risks: No offline grading path (blocks the exhibition's offline/unattended requirement outright for real GDPval scoring); reference files (audio/video/CAD) are heavier than a 2.6B-31B free local-like model can meaningfully consume; unbounded step count makes the 50-call/day free cap a first-order constraint; would need a custom Inspect Solver to plug in pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex.

candidates.name: TheAgentCompany (TAC)
candidates.task_shape: 175 tasks across 6 professional roles (Software Engineer, Product Manager, Data Scientist, HR, Finance, Admin), inside a simulated company: local workspace + intranet running real GitLab, ownCloud, Plane (project mgmt), RocketChat (messaging) instances the agent must browse/use/message through. Closest analogue to a full 'office environment with real tools and data,' not just files in a folder.
candidates.grading: Per-task Docker image with /utils/eval.py: dual-layer -- deterministic result-based checks plus encrypted (.enc, key-gated) LLM-based sub-checkpoint evaluators for partial credit. Requires an LLM configured via env vars for the LLM-based checkpoints.
candidates.official_protocol: Official harness = the repo's own Docker-based runner; first-class integration with OpenHands as the agent. Task structure per image: /utils (evaluator.py.enc, init.sh, config.py, common.py, eval.py), /instruction/task.md, /workspace. init.sh initializes the environment; eval.py is the grading entrypoint.
candidates.size_and_versions: 175 task images. README states verbatim: '30+ GB of free disk space' required; baseline tested on Amazon EC2 t3.2xlarge.
candidates.requirements: Docker + docker-compose mandatory (GitLab/ownCloud/Plane/RocketChat containers). 30GB+ disk alone exceeds our ~18GB total shared budget for this container -- a full run is out; a pruned subset (tasks touching only 1-2 services) is unmeasured and would need an actual trial, not an assumption.
candidates.supported_agents: First-class OpenHands integration with a dedicated evaluation harness. Generic Docker-reachable agents are theoretically compatible (the intranet exposes ports any HTTP/git-capable client could hit) but there is no documented pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex adapter -- would require writing one, similar in spirit to Harbor's installed-agent wrappers noted in the sibling scout-coding pass.
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not found this pass; TAC's published headline numbers in the paper focus on frontier models and note the benchmark is very hard overall (low completion rates even for strong models) -- no specific <=35B open-weight numbers surfaced.
candidates.fit: Strong conceptual fit for 'zero-config accountability in a realistic multi-app office job,' and its dual-layer (deterministic + LLM-checkpoint) grading is architecturally close to what an accountability check needs (localized pass/fail per sub-goal). But the disk requirement is a hard blocker as currently scoped.
candidates.cost_time: Not measured this pass (would depend heavily on the task and how many tool/intranet round-trips the agent takes); the published paper notes TAC tasks are long-horizon and multi-turn by design, so free-tier call budget per task is a real concern once disk is solved.
candidates.risks: 30GB+ disk requirement exceeds the whole session's shared budget outright; no ready pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex adapter exists; LLM-based sub-checkpoint evaluators need a configured judge model (not specified as free/local by default).

candidates.name: OfficeBench
candidates.task_shape: 300 tasks (single/two/three-application scenarios) across Word, Excel, PDF, email, and calendar; the agent must chain operations across multiple office apps to satisfy one workflow -- the closest thing found to 'use the logo file, the schedule file, and the data file together' at office-document granularity.
candidates.grading: No LLM judge at all -- Exact Matching, Fuzzy Matching, and Execution-based Evaluation, fully local and deterministic, per the repo/paper's own description.
candidates.official_protocol: Repo setup via conda + per-model config files (OpenAI/Gemini/vLLM backends) and Docker for the office-app sandboxes. Best published baseline: GPT-4o at 47.00% pass rate (their own headline number) -- hard even for a frontier model, leaving visible headroom for a small free model to score lower, which is exactly the shape a 'with vs without Vacant' comparison needs.
candidates.size_and_versions: 300 tasks total across the 3 scenario complexities; repo does not state an explicit dataset size in the README content read this pass.
candidates.requirements: Docker for app sandboxes; conda environment; explicit disk size not stated (unverified, would need a local clone/measure before committing).
candidates.supported_agents: Unverified/unconfirmed: README language ('operations from multiple applications' within a 'transition system') suggests OfficeBench may drive the agent action-by-action itself as an evaluation harness rather than exposing a clean subprocess boundary a pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex CLI could be dropped into as-is -- needs a code-level read (not done this pass) before assuming compatibility.
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not found this pass; only the GPT-4o 47.00% headline number was surfaced.
candidates.fit: Best 3-way budget fit found (file-grounded multi-app tasks + zero-cost deterministic grading + presumably modest resource needs) but agent-interface compatibility with our 4 target harnesses is the single biggest open unknown and needs verification before this is actionable.
candidates.cost_time: No judge-model calls needed at all for grading, so the full 50-calls/UTC-day free budget is available to the agent under test; per-task call count not measured (would depend on how many app operations each of the 300 tasks needs, likely fewer than TAC/GDPval given the narrower app surface).
candidates.risks: Unconfirmed whether the harness can host an arbitrary CLI coding agent versus requiring its own action-execution loop; repo disk footprint and Docker requirements not independently measured.

candidates.name: OdysseyBench (microsoft/OdysseyBench)
candidates.task_shape: OfficeBench's long-horizon sequel: two splits, OdysseyBench+ (300 tasks derived from real use cases) and OdysseyBench-Neo (302 newly synthesized), same app surface (Word/Excel/PDF/Email/Calendar) but requiring the agent to extract essential context from a long-horizon interaction history rather than a single fresh file drop -- explicitly built on the OfficeBench codebase per its own description.
candidates.grading: Not independently confirmed this pass -- presumed to inherit OfficeBench's deterministic Exact/Fuzzy/Execution-based matching given the stated codebase lineage, but this was not verified against the actual repo code (flagged unverified).
candidates.official_protocol: Not independently verified this pass; would need the same code-level read as OfficeBench.
candidates.size_and_versions: 602 tasks total across the two splits (300 + 302); no independent size/disk measurement taken this pass.
candidates.requirements: Presumed similar to OfficeBench (Docker, conda) -- not verified.
candidates.supported_agents: Not verified this pass; same open question as OfficeBench.
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not found this pass.
candidates.fit: Its stated angle -- agent must recall context across a long interaction history, not just consume a fresh file drop -- is the one candidate whose research question most directly overlaps with Vacant's own trace/accountability concept (did the agent actually use what came before, is there an unexplained gap). Worth a second, deeper pass specifically if OfficeBench's agent-interface turns out workable, since this is essentially 'OfficeBench plus the part Vacant is built to check.'
candidates.cost_time: Not measured this pass.
candidates.risks: Everything below the task-shape description is unverified this pass (grading mechanics, disk footprint, agent-interface compatibility) -- treat as a lead, not a validated candidate, until a direct code read is done.

candidates.name: GAIA (Meta / HuggingFace / AutoGPT team)
candidates.task_shape: 466 questions across 3 difficulty levels (166 validation + 300 test). Many require opening an attached file (PDF, CSV, audio, image, zip) plus web/tool use to produce a short factual answer -- 'easy for a competent human, hard for an AI that must actually use tools.' A real given-materials-produce-a-grounded-answer task, but the deliverable is a short answer string, not a document -- weaker analogue to 'write the marketing plan' than GDPval/OfficeBench/TAC but far cheaper to grade.
candidates.grading: Quasi exact-match, fully deterministic, no judge model at all. Validation split (166) has public answers usable for local scoring; test split (300) is leaderboard-only with hidden answers.
candidates.official_protocol: No fixed scaffold -- any tool-using agent can be pointed at a question + its attached file(s) and its final short answer scored by quasi exact match. Official leaderboard is the HF Space above (submit a JSONL of predictions; test answers stay private).
candidates.size_and_versions: 110MB total dataset (per HF page metadata read 2026-09-25), stored as metadata.parquet + companion files referenced by file_path (e.g. under 2023/test/). 466 questions total, 3 levels.
candidates.requirements: Trivial disk footprint (110MB). Dataset is gated on HuggingFace -- requires accepting a 'do not reshare outside a gated/private HF repo' agreement before download, which brushes against this task's 'no sign-ups' constraint and should be raised with the lead rather than clicked through unilaterally.
candidates.supported_agents: Best fit of the 11 for zero-adapter-work compatibility with pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex -- no fixed scaffold, just 'give the agent the question + attached file, read back the final short answer.'
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not independently found this pass (would need a direct leaderboard read with model-size filtering); unverified.
candidates.fit: Strong budget/complexity fit (deterministic grading = zero judge cost, tiny download, no scaffold lock-in, easy to wire into any of the 4 target agents) but the deliverable (short answer) is a weaker visual/marketing-plan analogue and would be less compelling for a physical-exhibition side-by-side than a full document would be.
candidates.cost_time: Per-task call count not measured this pass but should be low relative to GDPval/TAC given the short-answer format and typically single-file grounding -- plausibly the cheapest candidate per task in terms of free-tier call budget, though unverified without an actual trial run.
candidates.risks: HF dataset-gating agreement conflicts with the stated 'no sign-ups' environment constraint and needs the lead's sign-off; short-answer format under-exercises multi-step deliverable production, which is central to the owner's own worked example.

candidates.name: AssistantBench
candidates.task_shape: 214 tasks (33 dev / 181 test): realistic, time-consuming web tasks (e.g. monitor a real-estate market, locate nearby businesses) requiring live browsing -- this is the weakest match of the group to 'materials given in a folder'; it's open-web research, not office-document work grounded in provided local files.
candidates.grading: Closed-form answers, automated scoring (accuracy, answer-rate, precision, exact-match). Test-set answers are held out ('hidden for now'); only the 33-task dev split has public answers, so only that split can be scored locally without a leaderboard submission.
candidates.official_protocol: Submissions go through a HuggingFace-hosted leaderboard portal; SeePlanAct (SPA), the paper's own agent, builds on SeeAct with added planning/memory. No fixed browser-sandbox requirement was confirmed this pass -- unverified.
candidates.size_and_versions: 214 tasks total (33 dev + 181 test), covering 525+ pages across 258 websites per the paper.
candidates.requirements: Needs live internet access to real, changing websites (reachable via the session's HTTPS proxy) -- by design these are described as 'time-consuming' tasks, so wall-clock time per task is a real concern, not independently measured this pass.
candidates.supported_agents: Not tied to a fixed scaffold; any web-browsing-capable agent (pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex with a browser/HTTP tool) could in principle attempt it, though no first-class adapter was found.
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not found this pass; the paper's own headline is that no model tops 26% accuracy, without a small-open-weight breakout surfaced.
candidates.fit: Only usable on the small 33-task dev split for local scoring; not a strong analogue to 'materials in a folder' -- files a distant secondary candidate rather than a core one.
candidates.cost_time: Unmeasured; 'time-consuming' web tasks plus live browsing implies potentially many tool calls per task (page loads, scrolls, searches), a real risk against the 50-calls/day free cap if each call also burns a model turn.
candidates.risks: Held-out test answers block full-scale local scoring; live-web dependency conflicts with the exhibition's offline-first requirement even if useful for a pre-exhibition study; per-task call count unmeasured.

candidates.name: FACTS Grounding (Google DeepMind)
candidates.task_shape: Single-turn: (user request + long document, up to 32k tokens) -> long-form grounded response. No multi-step agent workflow, no tool use, no multi-file workspace -- a QA/generation task, not an agentic one. Would only exercise the underlying model's grounding behavior, not Vacant's step-level hook-and-trace loop (there are no intermediate steps to trace).
candidates.grading: 3 closed frontier LLM judges per the paper (originally Gemini 1.5 Pro, GPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet); final score = average of judges' scores across examples, computed separately for eligibility and grounding-accuracy.
candidates.official_protocol: Public dataset (google/FACTS-grounding-public) for dev-style use; full leaderboard/test evaluation happens via Kaggle's hosted benchmark page, private test answers.
candidates.size_and_versions: Not independently sized this pass (unverified); public HF dataset exists but is described as a subset, with the full/private test portion held by Google/Kaggle.
candidates.requirements: Requires access to 3 paid, closed frontier judge models to reproduce official scoring -- not free, not open-weight, not runnable within the free OpenRouter tier's local-like models.
candidates.supported_agents: Not agentic at all -- single prompt/response call, no workspace, so 'agent compatibility' with pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex is not really applicable in the intended sense (a coding agent could be pointed at it trivially, but it wouldn't exercise multi-step tool use).
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not found this pass; leaderboard reported (from the blog) skews to frontier models (Gemini 2.0 Flash Exp 83.6%, Gemini 1.5 Flash 82.9%, Claude 3.5 Sonnet 79.4%, GPT-4o 78.8%) with no small-open-weight breakout surfaced.
candidates.fit: Poor fit for this study's core question -- no agentic/workspace shape to exercise Vacant's hook-and-trace loop, and grading needs 3 paid frontier judges. Only useful as background reading on how 'grounding' is formally defined elsewhere, conceptually adjacent to what an accountability check verifies.
candidates.cost_time: Cheap per-example on the agent side (single call) but grading needs 3 separate paid frontier-model judge calls per example, none free.
candidates.risks: No local/free grading path at all; task shape doesn't exercise multi-step accountability, which is the actual thing being tested.

candidates.name: DeepResearch Bench (RACE + FACT)
candidates.task_shape: 100 PhD-level research tasks (50 English / 50 Chinese) across 22 domains; agent produces one long research report from open-web research -- not from attached local files, so no materials-folder to ground against, unlike the owner's own worked example.
candidates.grading: Two pipelines: RACE (report quality, reference-based, 4-dimension rubric: comprehensiveness/insight/instruction-following/readability) and FACT (citation/claim verification against sources). Per the repo's own README changelog (read directly from the cloned repo, dated 11 May 2026): official evaluator was just switched from Gemini-2.5-Pro to GPT-5.5 for RACE and GPT-5.4-mini for FACT, after a bake-off against Gemini-3.1-Pro and Claude-Opus-4-7 on a 200-article human-annotated subset (human inter-annotator baseline 68.78%; GPT-5.5 scored 71.82% overall, best of the three). Dual-acceptance window for old+new evaluator closed 31 May 2026 -- as of the 2026-09-25 read date, only the GPT-5.5/GPT-5.4-mini path is current.
candidates.official_protocol: Repo's own run_benchmark.sh + deepresearch_bench_race.py / FACT pipeline scripts (scrape -> extract -> validate -> score, per the results/fact/ directory structure observed in the clone). API-key based, judge model configured via the repo's API-configuration docs.
candidates.size_and_versions: Cloned repo (code + cached results, no large media) = 200MB. 100 tasks total. Two named releases exist: DRB (this one) and a separate follow-up DeepResearch Bench II (arXiv:2601.08536, different focus, not evaluated this pass).
candidates.requirements: Paid GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.4-mini API access required to reproduce current official scoring; not covered by the free OpenRouter tier. No Docker/heavy environment needed otherwise -- the repo itself is lightweight.
candidates.supported_agents: Not tied to a specific agent scaffold -- any system that can produce a long-form markdown research report from a prompt can be scored; a coding agent (pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex) could act as the 'deep research agent' by browsing and writing the report file.
candidates.small_open_model_results: Repo's own results/ directory (in the clone) includes prior runs for e.g. claude-3-7-sonnet-latest as a tested system, not a small open-weight model; no <=35B open-weight numbers surfaced this pass.
candidates.fit: Reasonable as a 'produce a well-researched document' stress test but not file-grounded (open web, no materials folder), and its official judge just moved to paid GPT-5.5/GPT-5.4-mini, closing off free/local reproduction of the headline metric.
candidates.cost_time: Repo is light to clone/read (200MB) but real judging requires paid frontier-model calls per report (RACE + FACT are both LLM-pipeline-heavy, with FACT doing a multi-step scrape/extract/validate chain per the results/fact/ directory structure observed) -- not free-tier feasible for the grading side.
candidates.risks: Official judge is now closed/paid (GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4-mini) with no free/local substitute documented; task is open-web research, not file-grounded, so it under-tests the specific 'did the agent use the given materials' accountability question.

candidates.name: WritingBench
candidates.task_shape: 1,000 real-world writing queries across 6 domains / 100 subdomains; each query paired with 5 instance-specific evaluation criteria, and many queries include attached open-source materials (e.g. public financial statements, legal templates) the response is expected to use -- a genuine 'given materials, produce a grounded write-up' shape, but single-turn (prompt+materials in, text out; no multi-step tool/workspace loop, so it would exercise Vacant's materials-grounding check but not its multi-step trace/rerun machinery).
candidates.grading: Per-criterion 1-10 score + justification, via either an LLM evaluator (repo docs recommend Claude-3-7-Sonnet) or a dedicated open-weight 7B critic model. Critic reaches 83% agreement with human preference per the README's own reported number (not independently re-verified this pass).
candidates.official_protocol: 3-step workflow in the repo: (1) generate responses to queries, (2) score with evaluator/llm.py (LLM-as-judge) or the critic model, (3) aggregate scores. No Docker/company-simulation, no multi-turn agent loop.
candidates.size_and_versions: 1,000 queries. Critic model: AQuarterMile/WritingBench-Critic-Model-Qwen-7B, fine-tuned from Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct on a 50K SFT dataset; GGUF-quantized builds exist (e.g. mradermacher/WritingBench-Critic-Model-Qwen-7B-i1-GGUF) suitable for CPU inference on this container.
candidates.requirements: Lightweight -- no Docker, no simulated environment; the only heavier asset is optionally self-hosting the 7B critic (a few GB depending on quantization), which is well within the disk budget and can run on CPU (slowly) given no GPU is available here.
candidates.supported_agents: Trivial to point any of the 4 target agents at: feed the query + attached materials as the prompt/workspace, capture the text response, score with the critic. No adapter work needed since it's not agentic/multi-step.
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not found for the *task-taking* side (system-under-test) this pass; the notable small-model fact here is on the *judging* side -- the 7B critic itself is the small open model, used as a grader rather than a subject.
candidates.fit: Best cost profile of the whole set for a same-day study: free/local judge (no OpenRouter calls needed for grading at all, sidestepping the 50-calls/day cap on that side entirely), file-grounded tasks, no heavyweight environment. Weakest point is that the task shape (single prompt->response) under-exercises Vacant's core hook-and-trace machinery, which watches multi-step tool use -- good for a controlled 'materials-grounding' sub-experiment, not a full analogue of the marketing-plan example on its own.
candidates.cost_time: Agent side: 1 model call per task (single-turn), cheapest of all 11 candidates by a wide margin, well within the 50-calls/day free cap even for the full 1,000-task set spread over multiple days. Judge side: zero OpenRouter/API calls needed at all if the 7B critic is self-hosted; CPU-only inference on a 4-CPU/15GB box will be slow per call but is free and offline-capable, which matches the exhibition's own offline requirement.
candidates.risks: Single-turn task shape doesn't exercise multi-step accountability (no tool calls, no files-read trace) -- would need to be paired with something more agentic to fully test Vacant's loop; critic model's 83% human-agreement number is self-reported by the paper's own authors, not independently re-verified in this pass.

candidates.name: ResearchRubrics (Scale AI)
candidates.task_shape: Domain-diverse, open-ended research prompts (no local materials/files -- open-web/knowledge-based, not file-grounded) paired with 2,500+ expert-written rubrics (~2,800 human labor-hours), scored across 6 axes (synthesis, explicit requirements, communication quality, factual grounding, reasoning soundness, clarity). Even frontier deep-research agents (Gemini DR, OpenAI DR) score under 68% average rubric compliance -- substantial visible headroom.
candidates.grading: Default judge: 'Gemini 2.5 Pro via LiteLLM' (litellm_proxy/gemini/gemini-2.5-pro-preview-06-05 in the repo's own config), documented as swappable but not free/open by default. Grading runs via API (LiteLLM), not locally, with configurable concurrency (default 20) and retry/backoff.
candidates.official_protocol: Repo evaluates whether a markdown research report (already produced) satisfies per-task rubric criteria; rubrics dataset lives on HF (ScaleAI/researchrubrics per repo docs, not independently downloaded this pass).
candidates.size_and_versions: GitHub repo itself is small (5 commits observed); dataset (processed_data.jsonl) downloaded separately from HF, size not confirmed this pass.
candidates.requirements: Needs a configured LiteLLM-reachable judge (paid Gemini 2.5 Pro by default); no Docker/heavy environment for the grading step itself.
candidates.supported_agents: Not tied to a scaffold for the system-under-test (any agent that can write a markdown report works); swapping the default judge model is documented as supported but not demonstrated with a free/open alternative.
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not found this pass.
candidates.fit: Rubric-per-requirement grading is conceptually the closest thing found here to Vacant's own 'which steps were justified' check -- a rubric item is essentially a located accountability point, and the framework's per-axis breakdown (factual grounding, reasoning soundness) maps well onto the kinds of things Vacant's trace already flags. But it isn't file-grounded, and the paid Gemini-2.5-Pro default judge is a real cost/reachability barrier for a same-day free-tier study.
candidates.cost_time: Not measured this pass; grading is per-report against many rubric items, so plausibly several judge calls per report even before counting the agent's own generation calls -- likely nontrivial paid-API cost to reproduce faithfully.
candidates.risks: Paid default judge with no confirmed free/open substitute tried by the repo authors; no local materials/files in the task design, weakening the analogy to the owner's marketing-plan example; dataset size/license not independently confirmed.

candidates.name: Agent-as-a-Judge / DevAI (metauto-ai)
candidates.task_shape: 55 realistic AI-development (coding) tasks with 365 hierarchical requirements organized as a DAG (some requirements depend on others succeeding first, e.g. 'visualize results' depends on 'load data' succeeding). The system under test is any agentic coding system that can 'receive a human query' and 'output a workspace' -- README explicitly names Devin, OpenHands, MetaGPT, GPT-Pilot as example systems. This is a coding benchmark, not a knowledge-work/office one -- included here purely for its evaluation-design relevance, not as a runnable knowledge-work candidate.
candidates.grading: An *agent* (not a single LLM call) inspects the output workspace plus execution trajectory and checks off each of the 365 requirements individually, reporting pass/fail with reasoning per requirement -- architecturally very close to what Vacant's own locate/blame/feedback pipeline already does (locate -> check -> report, no single holistic score). Original paper reports agent-as-a-judge reaching 90-92% alignment with human consensus vs. 60-71% for plain LLM-as-judge on this same benchmark.
candidates.official_protocol: Repo expects benchmark/workspaces/{AGENT}/ and benchmark/trajectories/{AGENT}/ populated in a defined trajectory schema per task; judge agent then runs its own graph/search/read/ask modules over that workspace+trajectory. Default judge model not stated in the README section read this pass (unverified).
candidates.size_and_versions: 55 tasks, 365 hierarchical requirements total (DAG-structured).
candidates.requirements: Needs a coding agent capable of producing a full output workspace + a captured execution trajectory in the repo's schema; disk/compute requirements for the judge-agent's own multi-step inspection not specified in the README content read this pass.
candidates.supported_agents: Explicitly designed to accept arbitrary agentic coding systems (named examples: Devin, OpenHands, MetaGPT, GPT-Pilot); no pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex adapter exists yet -- would need a small wrapper to capture workspace + trajectory in the expected schema, amount of adapter work unverified.
candidates.small_open_model_results: Not found this pass; README/paper snippets read this pass didn't specify a small-open-weight judge or system-under-test result.
candidates.fit: Not a task-shape match for this scout's brief (55 coding tasks, not knowledge-work-with-materials) so it doesn't directly answer the question asked -- but it is the strongest conceptual precedent found in this pass for 'requirement-level, located feedback beats a single holistic self-review score,' which is exactly Vacant's own thesis and worth citing in write-ups independent of whether DevAI itself ever gets run.
candidates.cost_time: Not measured this pass; the judge itself is agentic (multiple internal calls per requirement check across 365 requirements), so likely to be call-heavy relative to a single-shot LLM judge even before counting the system-under-test's own calls.
candidates.risks: Wrong domain for this scout's brief (coding, not knowledge-work) -- flagging explicitly so the lead doesn't mistake it for a direct candidate; default judge model and adapter effort both unverified this pass.

candidates.name: SpreadsheetBench (NeurIPS 2024 D&B)
candidates.task_shape: NL instruction + one or more input .xlsx files in a workspace; agent must produce an output workbook whose cell values/formats match a gold answer file. Real Excel-forum questions.
candidates.grading: Deterministic, OJ-style. `evaluation/evaluation.py` does per-cell value compare (numeric round-to-2dp, datetime->Excel-serial normalization) plus fill/font-color compare; a solution passes only if it matches ALL ~3 test-case spreadsheets for that question. No LLM judge. Not hidden from the agent (agent never sees the grader, only produces the output file).
candidates.official_protocol: LLM writes Python (openpyxl/pandas-style) code executed inside a provided Docker image against a Jupyter kernel server (`start_jupyter_server.sh`); output workbook scored by `evaluation.py` after `open_spreadsheet.py` forces recalculation via LibreOffice (`soffice` 7.5+) or win32com. Two modes: single-round (1 model call/task) and multi-round ReAct (`inference_multiple.py`, `--max_turn_num` default 5, confirmed inference_multiple.py:138).
candidates.size_and_versions: 912 real questions / 2,729 test cases (~3/question), all public in-repo tarballs: `sample_data_200.tar.gz` (200), `spreadsheetbench_912_v0.1.tar.gz` (full, 2025/04), `spreadsheetbench_verified_400.tar.gz` (expert-annotated 400-subset, 2025/12). A newer, harder successor 'SpreadsheetBench 2' exists (arXiv:2606.29955, 2026) — different benchmark, not this one.
candidates.requirements: Docker (code exec image), LibreOffice `soffice` (recalculation before scoring — not confirmed present in this container, must check), Python deps in requirements.txt (openpyxl, pandas, tqdm). No GPU. No external creds.
candidates.supported_agents: Official harness is its own inference/eval scripts (not pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex natively); any OpenAI-compatible client (incl. OpenRouter base_url swap) can drive the single-round or ReAct loop since the harness just needs a chat-completions endpoint. A generic file-workspace coding agent (bash+python) could do the task shape directly without the bespoke harness, but then would not be 'run exactly the official way' — using the harness's own inference scripts pointed at OpenRouter is the closer-to-canonical path.
candidates.small_open_model_results: Original SpreadsheetBench paper's own open-source-model results table was NOT confirmed in this pass (WebFetch of the arXiv page returned only the abstract, not full table body) — unverified, flagged for follow-up. A separate 2026 paper, Spreadsheet-RL (arXiv:2605.22642), reports open Qwen3 baselines: Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 / Qwen3-4B / Qwen3-8B / Qwen3-14B / Qwen3-32B in the 9.3-17.6% Pass@1 range, RL-tuned Qwen3-4B-Thinking-2507 12.0% -> 23.4%. Caveat: unverified whether that number is on this benchmark or on the newer SpreadsheetBench-2 (arXiv:2606.29955) — do not cite as same-benchmark without confirming.
candidates.fit: Very good fit for the 'did it actually use my data or invent numbers' failure mode — task is literally read the given xlsx, compute, write an output xlsx, graded by exact cell diff. Good headroom for a small local-like model: single-round default gets 1 call/task; the multi-round variant is exactly the kind of 'push back with located feedback' loop Vacant's Stop-hook targets.
candidates.cost_time: 1 model call/task (single-round) or up to 5 (multi-round ReAct, default max_turn_num=5). At 50 free/paid-cheap calls/day this is ~50 single-round tasks or ~10 multi-round tasks/day; well within a 5 USD budget on qwen3.5-9b/gemma-3-12b pricing (~0.05-0.15 USD/M tokens) for dozens of tasks.
candidates.risks: xlsx cell-format comparison can be brittle to formula-recalc quirks (motivates the LibreOffice recalculation step); `soffice` availability in this container is unconfirmed; original-paper small-model table unverified in this pass so exact expected baseline score is not yet pinned down.

candidates.name: DABstep (Adyen + Hugging Face, 2025)
candidates.task_shape: 450+ multi-step data-analysis questions over payments CSV/JSON data plus a `manual.md` business-knowledge doc; split easy (single dataset, warm-up, 16% of tasks) / hard (multi-dataset, multi-step, 84% of tasks). Agent gets a data-files directory to iteratively query/compute over, files-based, no external DB.
candidates.grading: Fully deterministic, confirmed by reading `dabstep_benchmark/evaluation/scorer.py` directly: numeric extraction + tolerance compare (`math.isclose(rel_tol=1e-4, abs_tol=1e-4)` for small/percentage values, decimal-aware compare for larger numbers), list compare (split on `,`/`;`), fuzzy string compare (`difflib.SequenceMatcher`) fallback. No LLM judge. The 450-task `default` split's gold answers are withheld (hidden test set, official leaderboard grades against it); a 10-row `dev` sub-split ships with public gold answers for local iteration.
candidates.official_protocol: Baseline is Hugging Face `smolagents` CodeAgent with local Python-sandbox code execution; HF gives free users 1k free LLM requests/day via Inference API for baseline runs (separate cap from OpenRouter's 50/day). No fixed step cap for the baseline CodeAgent was found in this pass (unverified exact default max_steps); the HF blog reports total-dollar-cost per full 450-task run ($2-$435 by model) rather than calls/task.
candidates.size_and_versions: 450+ tasks total (16%/84% easy/hard split per Table 1 of arXiv:2506.23719); public `dev` sub-split = 10 tasks with gold answers; full `default` split's gold is hidden for leaderboard integrity.
candidates.requirements: Just files (CSV/JSON + manual.md) and a Python sandbox — no Docker required by the baseline, no external creds beyond whichever LLM endpoint is used. No GPU.
candidates.supported_agents: Official baseline is smolagents CodeAgent, not any of pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex natively; any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (OpenRouter) can be swapped in for the baseline's LLM client. A generic file-workspace coding agent can also attempt the task shape directly (read files, compute, answer) without smolagents, but that deviates from 'run exactly the official way'.
candidates.small_open_model_results: arXiv:2506.23719 Table 1 ('Performance of baseline models... Hidden Test Set') lists only two Llama rows: Llama 3.3 70B (Hard 3.70%, Easy 68.06%, >35B, for contrast) and Llama 3.2 1B (Hard 0.00%, Easy 1.39%) — the one truly small open model tested scores essentially zero on Hard and near-zero on Easy. No Qwen/Gemma/Mistral row was found in this table in this pass; unverified whether the live leaderboard Space has more small-model community submissions (WebFetch of the Space page did not render a static results table).
candidates.fit: Very good fit for the invented-vs-sourced-numbers failure mode — factoid answers must be derived from CSV/JSON + a business-knowledge doc, exactly the shape Vacant's evidence-based accountability targets. The genuinely hidden 450-task gold set (unlike most other candidates) is a real integrity property for a public side-by-side, but that split can't be self-graded locally; only the 10-task `dev` split can, which is thin for a demo.
candidates.cost_time: Per-task call count for the baseline CodeAgent is unverified/open-ended (agentic multi-step, no confirmed default cap) — budget conservatively (cap agent step budget at ~5-8 for a wrapper) and run the 10-item `dev` split (self-gradable, public answers) rather than the hidden 450-task default split for automatic scoring.
candidates.risks: For automatic grading without submitting to the real hidden leaderboard, must restrict to the 10-task public `dev` split; per-task call budget for the official baseline is not pinned down in this pass, so wall-time/cost for a full run is not precisely known ahead of time.

candidates.name: InfiAgent-DABench (ICML 2024)
candidates.task_shape: DAEval: NL data-analysis question over a given CSV file (e.g. correlation, mean, categorical count); agent must answer using a fixed '@AnswerName[value]' tag format so answers can be regex-extracted.
candidates.grading: Fully deterministic. `eval_closed_form.py` regex-extracts `@AnswerName[value]` tags (`extract_format`) and does exact string match or float compare within 1e-6 (`is_equal`); each named sub-answer scored independently; PSAQ/ABQ/UASQ metrics are aggregates over these booleans. No LLM judge.
candidates.official_protocol: ReAct-style Docker-based Python-sandbox pipeline (`pipeline/`, `pipeline/activities/eval.py`) or the simpler DA-Agent (`examples/DA-Agent`). The closed-form single-shot setting used by `eval_closed_form.py` is typically 1 inference call per question; the ReAct pipeline variant uses more but its default step count was not found in this pass (unverified).
candidates.size_and_versions: 603 questions / 124 CSV files total in the paper; publicly released validation set = 400 questions / 72 CSV files (README_eval.md); a held-out test set exists 'to avoid data leakage' per the repo README, and its status beyond that line is unverified in this pass.
candidates.requirements: Just CSV files + Python (pandas). Docker only for the fuller ReAct pipeline variant, not the closed-form single-shot path. No GPU, no external creds.
candidates.supported_agents: Not natively run by pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex; the closed-form eval script is agent-agnostic (any model that can emit the `@AnswerName[value]` tag format works), so a generic file-workspace coding agent given the tag-format instruction can be scored directly by `eval_closed_form.py` without needing InfiAgent's own pipeline.
candidates.small_open_model_results: arXiv:2401.05507 Table 6 (agent framework with reformatting step enabled, closed-form eval): Qwen-72B-Chat 59.92%, Qwen-14B-Chat 37.50%, Qwen-7B-Chat 27.27%, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 38.67%, Baichuan2-13B-Chat 9.34%, Baichuan2-7B-Chat 8.95%, CodeLlama-34B-Instruct 31.13%, CodeLlama-13B-Instruct 26.67%, CodeLlama-7B-Instruct 24.61%, DeepSeek-Coder-33B-Instruct 46.09%, Phind-CodeLlama-34B-v2 43.87%. Llama2-13B/70B rows not reported in the table read. All well below GPT-4's paper-quoted 78.99%.
candidates.fit: Good fit — CSV + closed-form NL question about it is exactly the on-topic 'did it read the file vs invent the number' test, and the cheapest of all candidates per task. License is CC BY-NC 4.0 on the data (research/demo fine; note for redistribution).
candidates.cost_time: As low as 1 call/task in the closed-form single-shot setting; 400 public validation questions comfortably sampled at ~40-50/day under the 50-call cap, or the full set spread over multiple days.
candidates.risks: CC BY-NC 4.0 data license restricts redistribution; held-out test set's public availability is unverified beyond the README's 'to avoid data leakage' note; ReAct-pipeline default step count also unverified (only matters if the richer multi-step variant is used instead of closed-form).

candidates.name: DA-Code (EMNLP 2024)
candidates.task_shape: Data-science coding tasks over provided files spanning Data Wrangling, Machine Learning, and Exploratory Data Analysis (incl. some plot/chart outputs); agent works in an agentic ReAct-like loop inside a sandbox.
candidates.grading: Task-type-dependent via `da_agent/evaluators/evaluation.py`'s `Evaluator` class, produces a `total_score` and a `result_type` bucket; most types (data manipulation, ML metrics) look like deterministic file/value diffing from the CLI surface (`--gold_dir`, `--eval_json`), but the 'plot' result-type (chart output) compares generated charts/files against gold artifacts by an unverified mechanism (not read in this pass) — flag as partially unverified-deterministic.
candidates.official_protocol: Requires Docker (agent and experiments run in a sandbox, per README). Runner `run.py` is an agentic ReAct-like loop with `--max_steps` default 20 (confirmed run.py:54) and `--max_memory_length` default 15 — up to 20 model calls/task by default, CLI-adjustable lower.
candidates.size_and_versions: In-repo `da_code/source` ships a 100-example sample; the full dataset (per paper, hundreds of examples) plus a separate `gold` directory require two public Google-Drive `gdown`-fetchable downloads (not gated, but off-repo).
candidates.requirements: Docker mandatory. Two off-repo Google Drive downloads (>100MB for full gold) for the complete set. `da_agent`'s own LLM client supports AZURE_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY/GEMINI_API_KEY env vars; routing to OpenRouter via an OpenAI-compatible base_url swap is the natural path but was not confirmed against the client code in this pass. No GPU needed.
candidates.supported_agents: Own agent framework (`da_agent/`), not pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex natively; would need either a thin shim routing calls through OpenRouter, or reuse of da-code's own agent loop pointed at OpenRouter's base_url (unconfirmed feasibility, not yet read in the client code).
candidates.small_open_model_results: arXiv:2410.07331 Table 3, the only rows <=35B: Deepseek-Coder-33B (overall score 10.8%, completion rate 31.9%, DW 9.1% / ML 22.1% / EDA 7.6%) and Mixtral-8x22B (overall 15.4%, completion 67.2%, DW 14.8% / ML 31.6% / EDA 10.2%). Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct (22.6% overall) and Deepseek-Coder-V2.5 (20.7%) are >35B/large-MoE, shown for contrast only. Small local-like open models complete well under a third of tasks.
candidates.fit: Good task-shape fit (data wrangling/EDA/ML/visualization over given files) but heavier than SpreadsheetBench/InfiAgent-DABench: Docker sandbox mandatory, up to 20-step agent loop by default, and own bespoke agent framework rather than bring-your-own-agent.
candidates.cost_time: Up to 20 calls/task by default (CLI-adjustable via --max_steps). At 50 calls/day that's ~2 tasks/day at the default cap, more if the step cap is lowered.
candidates.risks: Docker + two off-repo Google Drive downloads add setup friction; plot-type grading mechanics unverified (not confirmed purely deterministic); OpenRouter routing through da_agent's own client not yet confirmed to work without code changes.

candidates.name: DSBench (ICLR 2025) — data_analysis and data_modeling sub-arms
candidates.task_shape: data_analysis: 466 open-ended NL/table/image tasks from ModelOff, free-text answers. data_modeling: 74 tasks from real Kaggle competitions (train/test CSVs, predict against a competition metric).
candidates.grading: data_analysis: `compute_answer.py` uses an LLM judge (gpt-4o-2024-05-13 prompted 'output True or False') — NOT deterministic, fails the deterministic-grading requirement despite an on-topic task shape. data_modeling: per-competition metric scripts (70+ files like `titanic_eval.py`, `spaceship-titanic_eval.py`) via `score4each_com.py`, presumably standard Kaggle metrics (accuracy/AUC/RMSE) — this arm IS deterministic, no LLM judge for the score itself (individual metric files not opened in this pass).
candidates.official_protocol: data_analysis: model produces free-text/tabular answers, scored by a separate GPT-4o judge call per item (extra paid-model dependency distinct from the agent under test). data_modeling: standard ML pipeline (load data, feature-engineer, train, predict, submit) scored by the matching Kaggle-style metric script; no fixed step cap found in this pass (unverified), realistically many tool calls per task.
candidates.size_and_versions: data_analysis 466 tasks (ModelOff-sourced); data_modeling 74 tasks (real Kaggle competitions). Data acquisition friction: data_analysis needs eloquens.com or a pre-packaged Google Drive/HuggingFace zip (`liqiang888/DSBench`); data_modeling needs the Kaggle API/credentials or the same pre-packaged mirrors.
candidates.requirements: data_modeling needs Kaggle API credentials (or HF/Drive mirror) — an extra account dependency unless the mirror is used. data_analysis needs a GPT-4o key for grading regardless of which model is under test. No GPU strictly required (ML tasks are typically tabular, not deep-learning-scale) but a full Kaggle pipeline is compute-heavier than the other candidates.
candidates.supported_agents: No official bring-your-own-agent adapter identified in this pass for either arm; would need a custom wrapper agent with an explicit low max-turns to keep data_modeling's call count bounded.
candidates.small_open_model_results: No published small-open-model (<=35B) score table located for either arm in this pass — unverified/not found. Not pursued further given data_analysis fails the deterministic-grading requirement outright and data_modeling's per-task call count is itself unverified (likely tens of calls, expensive against the 50-call/day cap).
candidates.fit: data_modeling arm is a strong task-shape fit (train.csv/test.csv + beat-this-metric is a clean read-and-compute task) but heavy — not a quick few-tool-call task. data_analysis arm is on-topic but disqualified by its LLM-judge grading (adds an extra paid, non-agent-under-test model as a grading dependency, inconsistent with 'log everything, keep comparable').
candidates.cost_time: data_analysis: likely 1-3 inference calls/task + 1 GPT-4o judge call/task (extra cost outside the tracked agent-model budget). data_modeling: likely much higher call count for a full pipeline, unverified exact figure — risk of blowing the 50-call/day budget on 1-2 tasks.
candidates.risks: data_analysis's LLM-judge grading breaks the deterministic-grading requirement and introduces an untracked paid-model cost; data_modeling needs Kaggle credentials or a data mirror and has an unbounded, likely large, per-task call count.

candidates.name: BLADE (EMNLP 2024 Findings)
candidates.task_shape: 12 dataset + open-ended research-question case studies; agent must choose conceptual variables and a statistical model, then produce a statistically justified analysis — richer/more open-ended than a single-number answer.
candidates.grading: Hybrid, partly LLM-based. `blade_bench/eval/llm/conceptual_var_similarity.py` and `model_similarity.py` use an LLM to match the agent's chosen conceptual variables/statistical model against ground truth (open-ended choices don't reduce to exact string match); a separate deterministic `eval/metrics/calc_metrics.py` scores downstream numeric metrics. Not purely deterministic overall.
candidates.official_protocol: `pip install blade-bench`; the evaluation itself needs API keys for OpenAI/Gemini/Anthropic for its LLM-based similarity scoring (an extra paid-model dependency distinct from the agent under test).
candidates.size_and_versions: 12 dataset+research-question case studies (paper terms them case studies; repo README placeholder text not yet filled with a final N). README states a hold-out test set is 'coming soon' — as of the commit read, full ground truth is public, no hidden split yet.
candidates.requirements: Python package install; API keys for at least one of OpenAI/Gemini/Anthropic for the grading LLM (separate from whatever model is under test). No GPU, no Docker mentioned.
candidates.supported_agents: No official bring-your-own file-workspace-coding-agent adapter identified; pip package provides its own harness, not a pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex hook.
candidates.small_open_model_results: No published small-open-model (<=35B) score table located in this pass — unverified/not found; deprioritized before spending more search budget given the grading itself is partly LLM-judged.
candidates.fit: Moderate — task is 'given a dataset + open research question, write a statistically justified analysis,' richer than 'compute one number' and partly rewards LLM-judged scientific nuance, which is not the 'did you use the file' failure mode Vacant targets. Less on-target than the CSV/spreadsheet candidates.
candidates.cost_time: Not established in this pass (unverified) given the candidate was deprioritized on the deterministic-grading criterion before a full cost pass.
candidates.risks: LLM-judge grading component breaks strict determinism and adds a paid-model dependency for grading itself; only 12 case studies limits statistical headroom for any side-by-side; small size (12) also means little room to sample a subset.

candidates.name: DiscoveryBench (ICLR 2025, AllenAI)
candidates.task_shape: DB-REAL (hypotheses/workflows drawn from published papers across multiple domains) + DB-SYNTH (synthetic); agent must read provided data and derive/verify a scientific hypothesis.
candidates.grading: LLM-judge, confirmed by reading `eval/eval.py` directly: it imports `openai.OpenAI` and `run_chatgpt_query_multi_turn`; `get_score_from_answer()` computes an F1-style score for the 'var' (variable match) type from a GPT-parsed JSON (`sizeA`/`sizeB`/`intersection` fields the judge model itself produces) plus a binary 'context' score from a GPT multiple-choice-style answer. Not deterministic — requires an LLM call per scored item on top of the agent's own calls.
candidates.official_protocol: Data ships in-repo under `discoverybench/`; scoring pipeline is `eval/eval.py` calling a GPT judge model per scored item; no fixed step-count found for the agent side in this pass.
candidates.size_and_versions: DB-REAL + DB-SYNTH, both shipped in-repo; exact task counts not tallied in this pass (deprioritized early on the grading criterion).
candidates.requirements: OpenAI API key for the judge model (separate paid dependency from the agent under test). No GPU, no Docker required for the data side.
candidates.supported_agents: No official pi/OpenCode/Claude Code/Codex adapter identified; own harness only.
candidates.small_open_model_results: No published small-open-model (<=35B) score table located in this pass — unverified/not found; not pursued further given the grading itself requires a GPT judge call per item.
candidates.fit: Poor fit for the deterministic-grading requirement (same reason as BLADE) even though the underlying 'read data, derive a hypothesis' task shape is on-topic. Soft-excluded: the task brief's defining trait is deterministic grading, and this benchmark's scorer is an LLM judge by design.
candidates.cost_time: Not established (unverified) — deprioritized before a full cost pass; grading alone requires 1+ GPT judge call per scored item on top of agent calls.
candidates.risks: LLM-judge grading is not deterministic and introduces an extra paid-model dependency and potential judge-model drift/nondeterminism between runs, undermining a clean 'installed vs not' side-by-side.

candidates.name: FinanceBench (2023, Patronus AI)
urls: https://github.com/patronus-ai/financebench (cloned, large pdfs/ dir removed locally post-read to respect disk budget)
candidates.task_shape: Open financial-QA over provided 10-K/10-Q/8-K/earnings PDF filings; agent must extract or compute a financial figure and cite evidence — exactly the 'unsourced specifics' failure mode Vacant targets.
candidates.grading: The paper's own methodology is human review ('manually review their answers (n=2,400)', repo README abstract). No official automatic scorer/exact-match harness found in the cloned repo — only `evaluation_playground.ipynb`, a notebook for exploring model outputs against gold, not a scoring pipeline. Not deterministically self-gradable out of the box; this disqualifies it against the task's core requirement.
candidates.official_protocol: No formal inference/eval harness script found; the repo is primarily a dataset release with a JSONL of Q/A/evidence plus source filings. Third-party repos (VectifyAI/Mafin2.5-FinanceBench, aquib8112/FinanceBench_RAG) build their own automatic graders (often LLM-judge) on top — unofficial, not 'run exactly the way the paper/official repo runs it.'
candidates.size_and_versions: 10,231 total questions per the paper, but the open-source repo ships only a 150-question sample (`data/financebench_open_source.jsonl`) with gold `answer` + `evidence` strings; remaining ~10,081 questions' answers are not public (a CLOSED_SOURCE `dataset_subset_label` value in the schema confirms a held-back split).
candidates.requirements: Just the 150 public questions + their source PDFs (raw 10-K/10-Q/8-K filings, was in /pdfs/, removed locally to respect the disk budget after reading listed contents). No GPU, no Docker, no external creds for the data itself — but no deterministic grader ships.
candidates.supported_agents: No official agent harness/adapter at all beyond a notebook; any file-workspace coding agent could attempt the QA task directly, but there is no official way to score it automatically.
